Validation#

Each check below is a test of tests/validation/. It compares a computation with a reference that HydroModPy did not produce: a closed-form solution, a published MODFLOW 6 example, a manufactured solution, or a parameter that a calibration must find again.

For every check the page gives the reference and its equations, the threshold with the size of the signal it is read against, the value the last recorded run measured, the outcome, and the date and commit of that run. A skipped test is shown as skipped: it proves nothing. Where a threshold lets a known discrepancy through, the case says so in a warning box at its top.

The measures come from a results snapshot committed next to this page, docs/source/theory/validation_results.json. When the site is deployed, the results the nightly jobs uploaded for the branch, if any, replace older ones. Each case gives the date and commit of the run its numbers come from. “When the checks run” below lists the jobs, read from the workflow files, and the checks that no job runs.

57 test files, 93 test functions, 38 benchmark cases. The results snapshot holds 342 test results from 5 runs (2026-10-13 to 2026-11-04): 342 pass.

When the checks run#

Read from .github/workflows/. A job runs a file when one of its paths holds it and its marker expression accepts the markers of the file. A test marked petsc is skipped where petsc4py is not installed. The nightly jobs upload what they measured. The deployed page lays the latest nightly results of its branch over the snapshot committed with the documentation.

Case by solver#

Each cell shows how close a solver gets to the known reference of a case, in the last recorded run. It is the distance to the reference as a share of a scale of the case, so that cases and solvers can be compared: for the closed-form head and discharge cases, the head-profile RMSE (else the first error in the unit of the scale) over the head range of the reference, its largest drawdown, its initial discharge, the travel of its front or the peak recharge, whichever the case names; for transport, particle tracking and calibration twins, the largest relative error the test records; for grid convergence and manufactured solutions, |p - p0|, the distance of the observed order from the expected one (under 0.1, under 0.2, above). Four classes, from the best to a warning: under 0.1 %, 0.1 to 1 %, 1 to 5 %, 5 % and over. A red cross means the test failed: the error went beyond its threshold. ▲ means the error grew by more than 20 % since the previous recorded run of that test, ▼ that it fell by as much. pass is a check that records no distance to a reference: the asserts of the test decide. Hover a cell for the metric, its value, its threshold, the share of the threshold it used and, when two solvers share the row, how many times the best solver's error it is. The thresholds and their shares stay in the section of each case. skipped and not measured prove nothing. n/a means the solver cannot run that test: the reason shows on hover and in the section of the case. A blank cell no longer exists: a solver column is a result, not measured, n/a or, while its declaration is missing, undeclared. gap marks a known discrepancy that the threshold lets through; the section of the case explains it. other gathers the solvers outside these columns and the tests that name none. The columns are modflow_nwt, modflow6, modflow6_irregular_tri, modflow6_voronoi, boussinesq and boussinesq_local.

Closed-form solutions, steady state#

Steady Boussinesq circular-island piecewise-K case#

pass, known gap end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_localmodflow6_voronoi_generated

Known gap: modflow6_voronoi

Known gap. MODFLOW 6 on the Voronoi dual sits 0.12 to 0.17 m below the reference inside 120 m (radial RMSE 0.12 m). Two errors add up there. The K zone boundaries (70 m and 140 m) pass through node rings, so those cells straddle two zones and take an area-weighted K: without Newton the same input files give 0.076 m, the heads 0.08 to 0.11 m too low inside 120 m and 0.05 m too high on the 140 m ring. Under Newton, the saturation of the upstream cell lowers them further, first order on rings 10 to 30 m apart. Until 2026-10-12 the top was the DEM, and the full-thickness weighting of the Newton conductance raised the heads, which offset the straddled zones: 0.056 m. MODFLOW 6 now reads a computational top that gives every cell the same thickness, and that offset is gone.

Compared with: steady radial Boussinesq solution with concentric piecewise K.

\[\frac{1}{r}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}r}\left(r\,K(r)\,H\,\frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}r}\right)+R=0\]
\[U=H^2,\qquad U(r)=U(a)+R\int_r^a \frac{s}{K(s)}\,\mathrm{d}s\]

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc (SNESVI obstacle) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.031 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.044 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.96 m. PETSc and the default engine agree to 1e-3 m. The mesh has near-equilateral triangles of 10 m with a node ring on each K break (70 and 140 m) and on the coast, and one ring of ocean triangles held at the sea level. The ring mesh it replaces (16 sectors cut along one diagonal, half of its ocean triangles capped at the sea floor) read 0.22 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine (scipy_sparse on 3155 cells) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.031 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.044 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.96 m. PETSc and the default engine agree to 1e-3 m. The mesh has near-equilateral triangles of 10 m with a node ring on each K break (70 and 140 m) and on the coast, and one ring of ocean triangles held at the sea level. The ring mesh it replaces (16 sectors cut along one diagonal, half of its ocean triangles capped at the sea floor) read 0.22 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 10 m grid: radial RMSE 0.0282 m, max error 0.0546 m, spread 0.0817 m, and half the measured freeboard of 0.910 m. MODFLOW 6 reads a computational top that gives every cell of the layer the same thickness, so its Newton conductance is the one of MODFLOW-NWT, and the two sit at the same distance from the reference (NWT 0.0284 m). What is left is the error of the grid. On a 5 m grid the RMSE falls to 0.0166 m and the max error to 0.0349 m, for MF6 and NWT alike; the spread stays at 0.083 m and the freeboard drops to 0.755 m. Until 2026-10-12 the top was the DEM and the RMSE 0.111 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Measured values with a 10 % margin: radial RMSE 0.1205 m, max error 0.173 m, freeboard 1.99 m. Twice the azimuthal spread of 5.2e-5 m: every cell of the coast ring holds the sea level, so the rings are symmetric. The run reads a 1 m raster whose shoreline lies 1 m inside the coast ring (config_modflow6_voronoi.toml). The profile is read on the node rings (5 m bins). The freeboard is read on the land surface the run was given, at the 196 m ring. This case cannot see the DEM-top bias come back, since that bias lowered its error; the Cartesian islands and tests/integration/test_the_computational_top_changes_only_the_mf6_grid.py do. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: radial_profile.azimuthal_spread 1.1e-4 (measure 4e-6, the head closure is 1e-4 m, and the measure read 5.2e-5 on 2026-10-14 on the same mesh).
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi_generated: Twice the measurement: radial RMSE 0.0614 m, max error 0.0999 m, azimuthal spread 0.0626 m, and half the freeboard of 0.2816 m. The engine generates a Voronoi mesh of 3 721 cells over the square of the 10 m raster and puts a face on each K ring (70 m and 140 m, mirror pairs), so no cell straddles two zones: the 0.12 m of the dual of a triangulation (config_modflow6_voronoi.toml), where the rings pass through cells, drops to 0.06 m. What is left is the saturation error of the upstream cell under Newton. The spread is the error of a mesh without the symmetry of the node rings; the freeboard is lower than the structured grid's 0.91 m because a generated cell can sit a few decimeters above the coast. Measured 2026-10-14. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Already at twice the measure: radial_profile.azimuthal_spread 0.126 (measure 0.0626); radial_profile.rmse 0.123 (measure 0.0614); radial_profile.max_abs_error 0.2 (measure 0.0999).
  • Radial head-profile RMSE: modflow_nwt allows 0.35, 7 times the 0.048 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile RMSE: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.35, 7 times the 0.048 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile max abs error: modflow_nwt allows 0.7, 11 times the 0.063 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile max abs error: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.7, 11 times the 0.063 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Azimuthal spread: modflow_nwt allows 0.35, 3182 times the 0.00011 of modflow6_voronoi. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Azimuthal spread: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.35, 3182 times the 0.00011 of modflow6_voronoi. No reason is written for this difference.

Steady Boussinesq divide piecewise-K case#

pass, known gap end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Known gap: modflow6_voronoi

Known gap, only partly the K break. The west zone sits 0.026 m below the reference, 0.016 m on the triangle strip. Control on a lattice strip of 3 node rows and 16 m columns: with the breaks on cell edges RMSE 1.34e-2 m, max 1.73e-2 m; with the breaks through the cell nodes RMSE 3.15e-2 m, max 5.03e-2 m. The blending of K on straddling cells is the part that the edge alignment removes. The 1.3e-2 m left on aligned edges is a discretization error of the strip, shared with the triangle grid (RMSE 1.2e-2 m).

Compared with: steady 1D Boussinesq profile with west divide, east fixed head, and piecewise K.

\[U=h^2,\qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(K(x)\,\frac{\mathrm{d}U}{\mathrm{d}x}\right)+2R=0\]
\[\frac{\mathrm{d}U}{\mathrm{d}x}(0)=0,\qquad U(L)=h_e^2,\qquad U(x)=h_e^2+2R\int_x^L \frac{s\,\mathrm{d}s}{K(s)}\]

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 40-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: RMSE 8.3e-3 m, max error 1.1e-2 m. Both upstream-weight the saturated thickness between cells, a first-order scheme: refining the grid by 2 halves the error. The heads are posed where the model holds them, at the centers of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc VI on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 6.7e-05 m, max error 0.00011 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column center. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The run goes through the launcher. Before 2026-10-09 the strip had one diagonal everywhere and read a RMSE of 9.4e-2 m. The launcher stores one profile per column and the loader tiles it: the row spread is zero by construction. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default local engine on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 6.7e-05 m, max error 0.00011 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column center. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The run goes through the launcher. Before 2026-10-09 the strip had one diagonal everywhere and read a RMSE of 9.4e-2 m. The launcher stores one profile per column and the loader tiles it: the row spread is zero by construction. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the 176-triangle strip: RMSE 1.2e-2 m, max error 1.7e-2 m. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Measured values with a 10 % margin: RMSE 1.75e-2 m, max error 2.79e-2 m, at x = 115 m. The gap below explains why the margin is not 2x. Each cell is read at its node and the profile is the area-weighted mean per 10 m column, for the model and the reference alike. The west divide is a no-flow face, which the nodes of the face sit on. The row spread is the float noise of the area-weighted mean. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: head_profile.row_spread 1e-9 (measure 8.88e-16, float rounding of the area-weighted mean).

Steady Boussinesq fixed-head piecewise-K case#

pass, known gap end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Known gap: modflow6_voronoi

Known gap. A Voronoi cell that straddles a K break takes the area-weighted arithmetic K of its two zones, while the reference jumps sharply, so the error peaks at the breaks (+0.046 m at x = 285 m, -0.021 m at x = 115 m). Control on a lattice strip of 3 node rows and 16 m columns: with the breaks on cell edges (120 m and 280 m are edges) RMSE 5.6e-3 m, max 9.4e-3 m; with the breaks through the cell nodes (columns shifted by 8 m) RMSE 1.70e-2 m, max 5.17e-2 m, close to the irregular strip (1.87e-2 m, 4.59e-2 m). The triangle strip assigns K by centroid and does not blend.

Compared with: steady 1D Boussinesq profile with piecewise-constant K.

\[U=h^2,\qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(K(x)\,\frac{\mathrm{d}U}{\mathrm{d}x}\right)=0\]
\[U(x)=h_w^2+\left(h_e^2-h_w^2\right)\frac{\int_{x_{\min}}^{x}\frac{\mathrm{d}s}{K(s)}}{\int_{x_{\min}}^{x_{\max}}\frac{\mathrm{d}s}{K(s)}}\]

Steady Boussinesq hillslope-interception benchmark#

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: the exact steady free-boundary solution under Dupuit. Below the emergence point x_e the head is the land surface and seeps out; above it all the recharge flows through the aquifer and the water table meets the surface tangentially at x_e (322.4 m here).

\[R\left(x_e-x_{\min}\right)=K\,S\left(z_{\mathrm{top}}(x_e)-z_b\right),\qquad z_{\mathrm{top}}(x)=z_{\mathrm{toe}}+S\left(L-x\right)\]
\[\left(h-z_b\right)^2=\left(z_{\mathrm{top}}(x_e)-z_b\right)^2+\frac{R}{K}\left[\left(x_e-x_{\min}\right)^2-\left(x-x_{\min}\right)^2\right]\quad (x<x_e),\qquad h=z_{\mathrm{top}}\quad (x\ge x_e)\]

Measured on 2026-10-13, commit 7c78961c6 with uncommitted changes, version 2.0.0a5, a local run. The last column gives the measured value and the threshold as shares of the head range of the reference, 2.66 to 2.66 m.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of boussinesq: PETSc VI, the boussinesq variant, against the exact seepage-face solution, started from the outlet head over the whole hillslope. SNESVI converges in 31 iterations (residual 9.8e-11 m3/s). Head profile: RMSE 0.0066 m, max 0.0375 m in the column that holds the tangent point x_e = 322.4 m, the dry zone within 2e-5 m; bounds twice the measurement. The contact point is read on 10 m columns with a 5 cm tolerance, as on the reference (281.6 m): measured 3.4 m off, the bound sits half a column above and fails on the next column. The head may not exceed the land surface by more than the solver closure (1e-6 m). Row spread: 9e-16 m measured, bound 1e-8 m. Until 2026-10-09 the reference ignored the seepage face and the solve started from that reference and stopped at 20 iterations.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: The default local engine, regularized partition closure, against the exact seepage-face solution, started from the outlet head over the whole hillslope, with the Newton closure of config_boussinesq_local.toml (1e-8 m3/s): 12 iterations. Head profile: RMSE 0.0071 m, max 0.0375 m in the column that holds the tangent point, as PETSc; the dry heads sit 0.003 m low, the partition releasing a little water where the water table is within a few of its 0.05 m depth scale of the surface. Bounds twice the measurement. The contact point, read on 10 m columns with a 5 cm tolerance as on the reference, is 3.4 m off: the bound sits half a column above. Row spread 1.9e-7 m, bound twice that. The head may not exceed the land surface by more than 1e-6 m. Until 2026-10-10 the release scaled with the saturated share of the cell: RMSE 0.0105 m, dry heads 0.009 m low.
  • Thresholds of modflow6: MODFLOW 6, 40 x 3 cells of 10 m, the land surface a DRN of conductance K * area / b with b = 1 m, against the exact seepage-face solution; same model, same numbers as MODFLOW-NWT. Head profile: RMSE 6.6e-3 m, max 8.6e-3 m; bounds twice the measurement. The dry heads sit 8.5e-3 m low, the error of placing the free boundary on a 10 m cell (first order in the cell, as for NWT). The contact point, read on 10 m columns with a 5 cm tolerance (281.6 m), is 3.4 m off: bound twice that. The DRN lets the head stand above the surface by (R + K S^2) b / K = 3.9e-4 m (measured 3.9e-4 m): bound twice the measure. Row spread 2.3e-9 m measured (the IMS closes at 1e-9 m), bound 5e-9 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: MODFLOW 6 on 586 irregular triangles of about 6 m (DISV), the land surface a DRN of conductance K * area / b with b = 1 m, so the leakance K / b is the same on every triangle. The surface comes from a 2.5 m raster, so no flat strip lies along the east face (on a 10 m raster the last 10 m column stood 4.1e-3 m above the reference, its end cells 8.6e-3 m above the surface). The east head, 5.0214 m, is the surface at the mean centroid of the two boundary triangles. The reference is evaluated at each centroid and averaged over the same 10 m bins as the model. Head profile: RMSE 2.0e-3 m, max 3.0e-3 m, dry heads 2.6e-3 to 3.0e-3 m low (the free boundary is placed to the cell); bounds twice the measurement. The contact point (281.6 m, 5 cm tolerance, 10 m bins) is 3.4 m off: bound twice that. Head above the surface (R + K S^2) b / K = 3.9e-4 m, measured 4.1e-4 m: bound twice the measure. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: MODFLOW 6 on the 315-node Voronoi dual of the same triangles, one cell per node, the land surface a DRN of conductance K * area / b with b = 1 m. The surface is sampled at the nodes from a 2.5 m raster, and the east head, 5.015625 m, is the surface on the three nodes at x = 400 m. Each cell is read at its node, and the profile is the area-weighted mean per 10 m column for the model and the reference alike. Head profile: RMSE 4.0e-3 m, max 5.2e-3 m, dry heads 5.2e-3 m low; bounds twice the measurement. The contact point (281.6 m) is 3.4 m off: bound twice that. The head stands above the surface by 4e-4 m on the seepage face, and by 2.4e-3 m in the last column, where the three held nodes take the whole outflow: the node 3.4 m from the face stands 6.1e-3 m above the surface, the nodes 7 m away 1.5e-3 to 2e-3 m. Bound twice the largest. The row spread is zero by construction. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Tightened to twice the measure: profile.rmse 0.0081 to 0.00806 (measure 0.00403); contact.max_positive_clearance_m 0.0048 to 0.00473 (measure 0.00236). Already at twice the measure: profile.max_abs_error 0.0105 (measure 0.00525); interception.x_error_m 6.8 (measure 3.4). Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: uniformity.row_spread 1e-9 (measure 8.88e-16, float rounding of the area-weighted mean).
  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt: MODFLOW-NWT, 40 x 3 cells of 10 m, the land surface a DRN of conductance K * area / b with b = 1 m, against the exact seepage-face solution. The surface is sampled at the cell centers and the east head is the surface at the center of the last column (5.0625 m, x = 395 m). Head profile: RMSE 6.6e-3 m, max 8.6e-3 m; bounds twice the measurement. The dry heads sit 8.5e-3 m low at the divide, and the offset fades to zero at the tangent point: the free boundary is placed to the cell, and the error halves with the cell (4.2e-3 m at 5 m, measured). It is not the drain: with b = 0.01 m the dry offset stays 8.7e-3 m. The contact point is read on 10 m columns with a 5 cm tolerance as on the reference (281.6 m): measured 3.4 m off, bound twice that. The DRN lets the head stand above the surface by the head that passes what the face drains, the recharge plus the through flow lost to the slope, (R + K S^2) b / K = 3.9e-4 m (measured 3.9e-4 m, 3.8e-6 m with b = 0.01 m): bound twice the measure. Row spread is zero by construction of the rows; bound 1e-9 m.

Steady sloping-substratum constant-thickness case#

pass, known gap end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Known gap: modflow6_voronoi

Known gap, 17 times the triangle strip (RMSE 4.0e-4 m). The reference is the uniform flow at constant thickness, which a flux error of a few tenths of a percent bends into a thickness drift of 0.03 m over the strip. The flux error comes from the face of the strip. The mesh bundle holds 3 face nodes 25 m apart, so the Voronoi cells of three interior nodes (x = 10.5, 388 and 390 m) own 2.6, 1.0 and 4.5 m of the held face, a no-flow edge there, and only the face nodes hold the head. Controls with the same case: the same nodes on a new Delaunay triangulation, RMSE 7.08e-3 m and max 1.49e-2 m, unchanged; face nodes added every 5 m so that they own the whole face, RMSE 8.4e-4 m and max 1.3e-3 m; a raster of 400 columns instead of 40, which removes the bilinear clamp in the half column at the ends, RMSE 7.05e-3 m and max 1.49e-2 m, unchanged. So the clamp is not the cause.

Compared with: exact steady profile H(x) = z_b(x) + b* with b* = 8 m.

\[H(x)=z_b(x)+b^\ast,\qquad z_b(x)=z_{b,0}+\Delta z_b\left(1-\frac{x-x_{\min}}{L}\right)\]
\[q=-K\,b^\ast\,\frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}x}=K\,b^\ast\,S_0,\qquad S_0=\frac{z_b(x_{\min})-z_b(x_{\max})}{L}\]

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt: Equal end thicknesses carry a uniform flow at constant thickness, which both conductance formulations reproduce exactly on a column grid. What is left is the solver closure. Twice the MODFLOW-NWT measurement with the validation profile (head closure 1e-9 m): RMSE 2.7e-7 m, max error 4.6e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Equal end thicknesses carry a uniform flow at constant thickness, which the solver reproduces exactly; what is left is the solver closure. Twice the measurement, PETSc and the local engine alike: RMSE 4.5e-07 m, max error 6.3e-07 m. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Equal end thicknesses carry a uniform flow at constant thickness, which the solver reproduces exactly; what is left is the solver closure. Twice the measurement, PETSc and the local engine alike: RMSE 4.5e-07 m, max error 6.3e-07 m. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6: MODFLOW 6 stops at its default head closure of 1e-4 m, and the error of this exact case is that closure. Twice the measurement: RMSE 8.3e-5 m, max error 1.2e-4 m. MODFLOW-NWT closes at 1e-9 m and reads 2.7e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the 176-triangle strip: RMSE 4.0e-4 m, max error 2.5e-3 m. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Measured values with a 10 % margin: RMSE 7.08e-3 m, max error 1.49e-2 m, at x = 375 m. The gap below explains why the margin is not 2x. Each cell is read at its node and the profile is the area-weighted mean per 10 m column, for the model and the reference alike. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: head_profile.row_spread 1e-9 (measure 1.78e-15, float rounding of the area-weighted mean).

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 40-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: RMSE 1.5e-2 m, max error 2.1e-2 m. Both upstream-weight the saturated thickness between cells, a first-order scheme: refining the grid by 2 halves the error. The heads are posed where the model holds them, at the centers of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc VI on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 8.5e-05 m, max error 0.0003 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column center. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default local engine on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 8.5e-05 m, max error 0.0003 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column center. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the 176-triangle strip: RMSE 1.6e-2 m, max error 2.4e-2 m. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Twice the error measured on the 101-node Voronoi dual of the triangle strip: RMSE 1.54e-2 m, max error 2.80e-2 m, against 1.57e-2 m and 2.36e-2 m on the triangle strip. Each cell is read at its node and the profile is the area-weighted mean per 10 m column, for the model and the reference alike. The row spread is the float noise of the area-weighted mean. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Tightened to twice the measure: head_profile.rmse 0.031 to 0.0308 (measure 0.0154). Already at twice the measure: head_profile.max_abs_error 0.056 (measure 0.028). Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: head_profile.row_spread 1e-9 (measure 1.78e-15, float rounding of the area-weighted mean).

Known gap: modflow6_voronoi

Known gap. A Voronoi cell that straddles a K break takes the area-weighted arithmetic K of its two zones, while the reference jumps sharply, so the error peaks just east of the first break (-0.024 m at x = 135 m). Control on a lattice strip of 3 node rows and 16 m columns: with the breaks on cell edges RMSE 6.6e-3 m, max 9.8e-3 m; with the breaks through the cell nodes RMSE 1.86e-2 m, max 3.33e-2 m.

Compared with: steady 1D Boussinesq profile with uniform recharge and piecewise K.

\[U=h^2,\qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(K(x)\,\frac{\mathrm{d}U}{\mathrm{d}x}\right)+2R=0\]
\[U(x)=h_w^2+C\int_{x_{\min}}^{x}\frac{\mathrm{d}s}{K(s)}-2R\int_{x_{\min}}^{x}\frac{s\,\mathrm{d}s}{K(s)}\]

What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column center. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The run goes through the launcher. Before 2026-10-09 the strip had one diagonal everywhere and the recharge mound came out 7 cm too high (RMSE 4.5e-2 m): the x conductance was about 7 % low. The launcher stores one profile per column and the loader tiles it: the row spread is zero by construction. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the 176-triangle strip: RMSE 7.6e-3 m, max error 1.5e-2 m. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Measured values with a 10 % margin: RMSE 1.12e-2 m, max error 2.40e-2 m, at x = 135 m. The gap below explains why the margin is not 2x. Each cell is read at its node and the profile is the area-weighted mean per 10 m column, for the model and the reference alike. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.

Steady circular-island 2D case using the ocean boundary condition#

pass, known gap end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Known gap: modflow6_voronoi

Known gap. MODFLOW 6 on the Voronoi dual sits up to 0.08 m below the reference inside 120 m (radial RMSE 0.067 m), where MODFLOW-NWT on the Cartesian grid sits 0.050 m away. MODFLOW 6 reads a computational top that gives every cell the same thickness, so the full-thickness weighting of its Newton conductance is gone. What is left is the saturation of the upstream cell, first order on 625 cells whose node rings are 10 to 30 m apart: without Newton the same input files give 0.003 m, the heads within 4 mm of the reference.

Compared with: steady radial Dupuit-Boussinesq solution with fixed coastal head.

\[\frac{1}{r}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}r}\left(r\,K\,H\,\frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}r}\right)+R=0\]
\[H(r)^2=H(a)^2+\frac{R}{2K}\left(a^2-r^2\right)\]
\[h(r)=z_b+\sqrt{\left(h_{\mathrm{sea}}-z_b\right)^2+\frac{R}{2K}\left(a^2-r^2\right)}\]

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc (SNESVI obstacle) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.033 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.055 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.90 m. PETSc and the default engine agree to 1e-3 m. The mesh has near-equilateral triangles of 10 m, a node ring on the coast and one ring of ocean triangles held at the sea level. Until 2026-10-09 it was a ring mesh of 18 sectors cut along one diagonal: there the two-point flux sat 0.25 m high with the reference imposed beyond 180 m, and refining that mesh made it worse (+1.1 m at 1476 and 5832 cells), while near-equilateral meshes converge (+0.08, +0.07, +0.02 m at 257, 886, 3147 cells). Half of its ocean triangles were capped at the sea floor (-1 m), a coastal sink that hid most of that bias.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine (scipy_sparse on 3147 cells) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.033 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.055 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.90 m. PETSc and the default engine agree to 1e-3 m. The mesh has near-equilateral triangles of 10 m, a node ring on the coast and one ring of ocean triangles held at the sea level. Until 2026-10-09 it was a ring mesh of 18 sectors cut along one diagonal: there the two-point flux sat 0.25 m high with the reference imposed beyond 180 m, and refining that mesh made it worse (+1.1 m at 1476 and 5832 cells), while near-equilateral meshes converge (+0.08, +0.07, +0.02 m at 257, 886, 3147 cells). Half of its ocean triangles were capped at the sea floor (-1 m), a coastal sink that hid most of that bias.
  • Thresholds of modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 10 m grid: radial RMSE 0.0499 m, max error 0.0921 m, spread 0.112 m, and half the measured freeboard of 0.787 m. MODFLOW 6 reads a computational top that gives every cell of the layer the same thickness, so its Newton conductance is the one of MODFLOW-NWT, and the two sit at the same distance from the reference (NWT 0.0495 m). What is left is the error of the grid. On a 5 m grid the RMSE falls to 0.0349 m and the max error to 0.0606 m, for MF6 and NWT alike; the spread stays at 0.111 m and the freeboard drops to 0.69 m, the first land ring being closer to the coast. Until 2026-10-12 the top was the DEM, the conductance followed the full thickness of the cells, and the RMSE was 0.221 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Measured values with a 10 % margin: radial RMSE 0.067 m, max error 0.080 m, freeboard 1.90 m. Twice the azimuthal spread of 9.9e-5 m: every cell of the coast ring holds the sea level, so the rings are symmetric. The run reads a 1 m raster whose shoreline lies 1 m inside the coast ring (config_modflow6_voronoi.toml). The profile is read on the node rings (5 m bins). The freeboard is read on the land surface the run was given, at the 196 m ring. Until 2026-10-12 the top was the DEM and the RMSE 0.102 m. Twice the error would let that bias back unnoticed, hence the 10 % margin. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: radial_profile.azimuthal_spread 2e-4 (measure 4.67e-6, the head closure is 1e-4 m, and the measure read 9.9e-5 on 2026-10-14 on the same mesh).
  • Radial head-profile RMSE: modflow_nwt allows 0.25, 5 times the 0.048 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile RMSE: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.25, 5 times the 0.048 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile max abs error: modflow_nwt allows 0.5, 8 times the 0.066 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Radial head-profile max abs error: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.5, 8 times the 0.066 of boussinesq. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Azimuthal spread: modflow_nwt allows 0.25, 1250 times the 0.0002 of modflow6_voronoi. No reason is written for this difference.
  • Azimuthal spread: modflow6_irregular_tri allows 0.25, 1250 times the 0.0002 of modflow6_voronoi. No reason is written for this difference.

PETSc Boussinesq variants on the steady Dupuit fixed-head case#

Not run on

  • NWT: The file runs the Boussinesq surface-interaction closures (regularized partition, complementarity, VI obstacle) selected through runtime_backend = petsc, which have no MODFLOW counterpart. The same Dupuit profile runs on NWT in test_dupuit_fixed_head_1d.py.
  • MF6: The file runs the Boussinesq surface-interaction closures (regularized partition, complementarity, VI obstacle) selected through runtime_backend = petsc, which have no MODFLOW counterpart. The same Dupuit profile runs on MF6 in test_dupuit_fixed_head_1d.py.
  • MF6 triangles: The file runs the Boussinesq surface-interaction closures (regularized partition, complementarity, VI obstacle) selected through runtime_backend = petsc, which have no MODFLOW counterpart. The same Dupuit profile runs on MF6 triangles in test_dupuit_fixed_head_1d.py.
  • MF6 Voronoi: The file runs the Boussinesq surface-interaction closures (regularized partition, complementarity, VI obstacle) selected through runtime_backend = petsc, which have no MODFLOW counterpart. A MF6 Voronoi run of this Dupuit profile belongs in test_dupuit_fixed_head_1d.py, not here.
  • Boussinesq default: The complementarity and VI obstacle closures exist only in the PETSc engine; the local engine supports head_only_regularized_partition only. The regularized-partition profile on the default engine is already test_dupuit_fixed_head_1d[boussinesq_local].

Compared with: Dupuit steady fixed-head solution.

\[\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(K\,h\,\frac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}x}\right)=0\]
\[h(x)=\sqrt{h_w^2+\left(h_e^2-h_w^2\right)\frac{x-x_{\min}}{x_{\max}-x_{\min}}}\]

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of petsc: Twice the error measured with this PETSc variant on 40 columns: RMSE 4.1e-05 m, max error 9.9e-05 m. No surface contact here, so the closures agree with the default Boussinesq variant to 1e-8 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column center. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of petsc_partition: Twice the error measured with this PETSc variant on 40 columns: RMSE 4.1e-05 m, max error 9.9e-05 m. No surface contact here, so the closures agree with the default Boussinesq variant to 1e-8 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column center. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.

Steady Dupuit seepage limit and its invariance in K/R#

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_localboussinesq_k_onlyboussinesq_local_k_onlyboussinesq_local_scaled_downboussinesq_local_scaled_upboussinesq_scaled_downboussinesq_scaled_upmodflow6_irregular_tri_k_onlymodflow6_irregular_tri_scaled_downmodflow6_irregular_tri_scaled_upmodflow6_k_onlymodflow6_scaled_downmodflow6_scaled_upmodflow6_voronoi_k_onlymodflow6_voronoi_scaled_downmodflow6_voronoi_scaled_upmodflow_nwt_k_onlymodflow_nwt_scaled_downmodflow_nwt_scaled_up

Compared with: Dupuit seepage limit x_e = L / (1 + slope**2 K/R) and the free Dupuit water table above it.

\[x_e=\frac{L}{1+s^2\,K/R}\]
\[h(x)=s\,x \quad (x<x_e),\qquad h(x)^2=(s\,x_e)^2+\frac{2R}{K}\left(L\,(x-x_e)-\frac{x^2-x_e^2}{2}\right) \quad (x\ge x_e)\]

\(s\) is the slope of the surface, \(L\) the length of the hillslope, \(x\) the distance upslope from the toe, \(K\) the hydraulic conductivity and \(R\) the recharge.

Measured on 2026-10-13, commit 7c78961c6 with uncommitted changes, version 2.0.0a5, a local run. The last column gives the measured value and the threshold as shares of the head range of the reference, 4.55 to 5.61 m.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow6, boussinesq_k_only, boussinesq_local_k_only, boussinesq_local_scaled_down, boussinesq_local_scaled_up, boussinesq_scaled_down, boussinesq_scaled_up, modflow6_irregular_tri_k_only, modflow6_irregular_tri_scaled_down, modflow6_irregular_tri_scaled_up, modflow6_k_only, modflow6_scaled_down, modflow6_scaled_up, modflow6_voronoi_k_only, modflow6_voronoi_scaled_down, modflow6_voronoi_scaled_up, modflow_nwt_k_only, modflow_nwt_scaled_down, modflow_nwt_scaled_up: MODFLOW 6, 80 x 5 cells of 5 m, the land surface a DRN of conductance K * area / b with b = 1 m. Measured, the seepage limit sits at 200 m (error 0) in the three scenarios of x_e = 200 m and at 135 m against 133.3 m for the doubled K (1.67 m, the 5 m column edge). Head profile: max error 8.2e-3 m, 1.17e-2 m for the doubled K. The K/R invariance holds to 1.3e-4 m (x 0.01) and 6e-7 m (x 100), the IMS closure being absolute. Doubling K alone leaves the drain outflow at R * area to 5e-7. The bounds are those of the original case, looser than twice the measure, and are left as they were.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: PETSc VI obstacle, the exact h <= z_top complementarity, on 320 triangles (80 columns of 5 m, 2 rows). It has no drain: a cell seeps when its head is within 1e-6 m of its surface, read on the mean of each 5 m bin, and the water that leaves is the surface-excess flux. Measured, the seepage limit sits at 200 m (error 0) in the three scenarios of x_e = 200 m and at 135 m against 133.3 m for the doubled K (1.67 m): bound twice that. Head profile: max error 2.1e-4 m, 7.0e-5 m for the doubled K; bound twice the largest. The K/R invariance holds to 8.9e-16 m, roundoff, and moves no cell: bound 1e-12 m. The absolute residual closure follows the recharge (1e-9, 1e-11, 1e-7 m3/s). Doubling K alone moves 26 cells and leaves the surface outflow at R * area to 5.8e-7, bound 1.2e-6. The flat start at 2 m above the surface converges in 30 iterations.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Default local engine, the regularized partition closure, on 320 triangles (80 columns of 5 m, 2 rows). The partition releases a little water wherever the water table is within a few of its 0.05 m depth scale of the surface, so a cell seeps when its head is within 1e-6 m of the surface, read on the mean of each 5 m bin, and the water that leaves is the surface-excess flux. Measured, the seepage limit sits at 200 m (error 0) in the three scenarios of x_e = 200 m and at 135 m against 133.3 m for the doubled K (1.67 m): bound twice that. Head profile: max error 4.2e-4 m, 8.2e-5 m for the doubled K; bound twice the largest. The K/R invariance holds to 1.8e-8 m and moves no cell, but only with the Newton closures scaled with the recharge (residual 1e-8, 1e-10, 1e-6 m3/s). Doubling K alone moves 26 cells; the release is 2.4e-4 of R * area off, bound 5e-4. From a flat start the dense Newton of the doubled K drives tens of toe cells below the bottom and its Jacobian solve fails (300 iterations, with a flat start from 0.5 to 10 m, the surface or an offset below it): the control starts from the solution of the reference scenario, 86 iterations to 1.8e-10 m3/s.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: MODFLOW 6 on 594 irregular triangles of about 6 m (DISV), the land surface a DRN of conductance K * area / b with b = 1 m, so the leakance K / b is the same on every triangle whatever its area. The 5 m raster the tops are sampled from is flat past the center of its end columns: the reference is read at the same positions, at each centroid, and averaged over the same 5 m columns as the model. Measured, the seepage limit sits at 200 m (error 0) in the three scenarios of x_e = 200 m and at 135 m against 133.3 m for the doubled K (1.67 m): bound twice that. Head profile: max error 4.7e-3 m, 5.8e-3 m for the doubled K; bound twice the largest. Three cells (the limit falls inside one column) differ from the seepage state of their column, as in the doubled-K scenario; bound twice that. The K/R invariance holds to 1.8e-7 m and moves no cell: bound 4e-7 m. Doubling K alone moves 107 cells and leaves the drain outflow at R * area to 1.1e-9, bound 3e-9. Needs the ILUT fill of the case config: with the stock fill the inner solves hit their cap.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: MODFLOW 6 on the 320-node Voronoi dual of the same triangles, one cell per node, the land surface a DRN of conductance K * area / b with b = 1 m. Each head sits at its node, so a column is the area-weighted mean of the cells whose node falls in it, for the model and the reference alike. The surface is sampled at the nodes from the 5 m raster, flat past the center of its end columns: the toe nodes at x = 400 m read 0.05 m, not the 0 m of the plane, so no cell is dry, and the reference is read at the same positions. Measured, the seepage limit sits at 200 m (error 0) in the three scenarios of x_e = 200 m and at 135 m against 133.3 m for the doubled K (1.67 m): bound twice that. Head profile: max error 8.6e-3 m, 1.23e-2 m for the doubled K; bound twice the largest. One cell differs from the seepage state of its column in the doubled-K scenario: bound twice that. The K/R invariance holds to 1.0e-7 m and moves no cell: bound 2e-7 m. Doubling K alone moves 57 cells and leaves the drain outflow at R * area to 3.7e-9, bound 8e-9. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Tightened to twice the measure: seepage_limit.head_profile_max_abs_error 0.025 to 0.0247 (measure 0.0123); seepage_limit.position_error 3.4 to 3.34 (measure 1.67). Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: control.drain_outflow_ratio_error 8e-9 (measure 3.35e-9, solver closure of the scaled system); invariance.head_max_abs_error 2e-7 (measure 9.93e-8, solver closure of the scaled system).
  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt: MODFLOW-NWT, 80 x 5 cells of 5 m, the land surface a DRN of conductance K * area / b with b = 1 m, in the four scenarios. Measured, the seepage limit sits at 200 m in the three scenarios of x_e = 200 m (error 0) and at 135 m against 133.3 m for the doubled K (1.67 m, the 5 m column edge): bound twice that. Head profile: max error 8.2e-3 m in the three, 1.17e-2 m for the doubled K, the cell-size error of placing the free boundary; bound twice the largest. The K/R invariance holds to 4.8e-7 m, the float32 resolution of the stored heads: bound 1e-6 m. This needs the run to use the NWT validation profile (headtol 1e-9 m, fluxtol 1e-10 m3/s) in every scenario; without it the scaled scenarios differ from the reference by 7e-3 m. Doubling K alone moves 65 cells and leaves the drain outflow at R * area to 1.3e-8, bound 3e-8. The quasi-1D rows agree.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

Three claims, in decreasing order of importance:

1. the seepage mask starts where the Dupuit closed form says it does, 2. scaling K and R by the same factor leaves the mask identical cell for cell and the head equal to a tight band - the property the whole calibration method rests on, 3. the same factor on K alone moves the mask, while the total drain discharge does not move at all.

Claim 3 is why claim 2 never looks at the discharge: mass balance pins the total drain outflow at R * area whatever the conductance does, so a discharge-based invariance check passes on a model that ignores K entirely.

Six solvers run it, each on four scenarios (the reference, K and R scaled down and up, K alone doubled): MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 on a structured grid, MODFLOW 6 on irregular triangles and on their Voronoi dual, with a drain at the land surface, and the in-house Boussinesq solver on its PETSc VI obstacle and its default local engine. A Boussinesq run has no drain: its seepage mask is read from the heads, and the water that leaves is its surface-excess flux.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 40-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: RMSE 6.6e-3 m, max error 7.9e-3 m. Both upstream-weight the saturated thickness between cells, a first-order scheme: refining the grid by 2 halves the error. The heads are posed where the model holds them, at the centers of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc VI on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 9.9e-05 m, max error 0.00015 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column center. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default local engine on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 9.9e-05 m, max error 0.00015 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column center. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the 176-triangle strip: RMSE 7.7e-3 m, max error 1.1e-2 m. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Twice the error measured on the 101-node Voronoi dual of the triangle strip: RMSE 4.5e-3 m, max error 1.31e-2 m. A side head sits on the cells seeded on the face, so the reference poses it on the faces. Each cell is read at its node and the profile is the area-weighted mean per 10 m column, for the model and the reference alike. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Tightened to twice the measure: head_profile.rmse 0.009 to 0.00896 (measure 0.00448); head_profile.max_abs_error 0.027 to 0.0262 (measure 0.0131).

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

The case runs through the launcher, the route of test_dupuit_fixed_head_1d.py, on copies of its configuration refined twice by 2 (cells of 25, 12.5 and 6.25 m). The slope of the head RMSE against the cell size is the observed order of the scheme.

Without Newton, MODFLOW 6 takes the harmonic mean of the two cell transmissivities, a centered scheme of order 2. A head posed half a cell away from where the reference expects it adds an error of order 1 and drops the observed order to 1. This is the check the MMS tests cannot make: they import nothing from hydromodpy.

Under Newton, the HydroModPy default, MODFLOW 6 weights the saturated thickness of the upstream cell, and so does MODFLOW-NWT. That scheme is of order 1 by construction: the RMSE halves when the cells halve (13.3, 6.7 and 3.4 mm here). Both runs are checked against order 1.

The same refinement runs on the other grids of the strip. The triangle and Voronoi grids are built in tmp_path from the uniform right-triangle strip (write_uniform_strip_bundle and write_gmsh22_triangle_mesh_from_bundle_csv), with dx = dy so that the centroid line across a diagonal stays normal to the edge; no bundle is committed. MODFLOW 6 on triangles and on the Voronoi dual observes the same orders as the structured grid, 2 without Newton and 1 under Newton (the upstream thickness weighting). The Boussinesq solver averages the thickness of the two cells in the edge flux, which is exact in h^2 at the centroids. Its second-order error is that of the aggregation: the profile is the column mean of the centroids at dx/3 and 2dx/3, read against the reference at the column center. PETSc and the default local engine give the same errors to 1e-9 m; the local engine goes from the dense solver (64 and 256 cells) to scipy_sparse (1024 cells at 64 columns) inside the refinement without moving the result.

Every run closes the head to 1e-9 m, far below the discretization error, so the observed order is the order of the scheme. The bands are those of the MMS orders, |p - 2| < 0.2 and |p - 1| < 0.2 (tests/TOLERANCES.md).

Rotated horizontal K tensor: uniform flow along a confined strip, plan view#

pass end to endmodflow6modflow6_mirrored

Not run on

  • NWT: MODFLOW-NWT reads K and Kv only: the load refuses K22 and the angles of the K tensor for it.
  • Boussinesq, Boussinesq default: The Boussinesq solver takes a scalar K: the load refuses K22 and the angles of the K tensor for it.
  • MF6 triangles: Not run: the case checks the tensor conventions on the structured grid. XT3D carries a linear head on triangles too (patch test), but this strip has no triangle variant.
  • MF6 Voronoi: Not run: the case checks the tensor conventions on the structured grid. A Voronoi variant of this strip is not set up.

Compared with: exact uniform flow of the rotated tensor, read in a window of +/- 100 m around the middle of the strip.

MODFLOW 6 turns the K11 axis by ANGLE1 = a from +x toward +y (Langevin et al., 2017, USGS TM 6-A55), so the tensor reads in the plane

\[K_{xx}=K_{11}\cos^2 a+K_{22}\sin^2 a,\quad K_{yy}=K_{11}\sin^2 a+K_{22}\cos^2 a,\quad K_{xy}=\left(K_{11}-K_{22}\right)\sin a\cos a\]

Far from the ends no water crosses the sides, so the exact head is a plane with

\[\frac{\partial h/\partial y}{\partial h/\partial x}=-\frac{K_{xy}}{K_{yy}},\qquad Q=\frac{K_{11}K_{22}}{K_{yy}}\left(-\frac{\partial h}{\partial x}\right)w\,b\]

where \(Q\) is the flow along the strip, \(w\) its width and \(b\) its thickness.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow6, modflow6_mirrored: Derived from the solver closure. XT3D carries a linear head exactly, so the window holds no discretization error: the errors do not fall with the cell size (head 3.5e-9 m on 10 m cells, 2.7e-7 m on 2.5 m cells), they follow the conditioning of the solve. What is left is the linear solve, closed at 1e-9 m, and end effects 22 decay lengths away. The bounds are about ten times the largest error of the four runs of the two K tensor cases, both signs. Measured here at +30 and -30 deg: gradient direction 2.2e-10 and 4.3e-9, head 3.9e-9 and 1.3e-8 m, end flow 4.2e-8 and 1.5e-7. A sign error on ANGLE1 gives a direction error of 2, the two-point flux without XT3D a direction error of 1 and a head error of 0.33 m.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

The flow sets K, K22 and ANGLE1 through [flow.param], HydroModPy writes them to the NPF package with XT3D, and the run stores the heads and the constant-head flows. A sign error on ANGLE1 flips the slope across the strip, an axis error changes its size, and the two-point flux without XT3D leaves it at zero: each moves the heads by a share of the 0.56 m drop across the strip. The mirrored variant runs ANGLE1 = -30 deg against its own reference.

Tilted K tensor: uniform flow along a confined layered section#

pass end to endmodflow6modflow6_mirrored

Not run on

  • NWT: MODFLOW-NWT reads K and Kv only: the load refuses the angles of the K tensor for it.
  • Boussinesq, Boussinesq default: The Boussinesq solver is a single-layer vertically integrated model with a scalar K: the load refuses the angles of the K tensor for it.
  • MF6 triangles: The section is one row of cells: the tensor tilts in the vertical plane, which a triangle mesh of the plan view does not change.
  • MF6 Voronoi: The section is one row of cells: the tensor tilts in the vertical plane, which a Voronoi mesh of the plan view does not change.

Compared with: exact uniform flow of the tilted tensor, read in a window of +/- 25 m around the middle of the section.

MODFLOW 6 turns the K11 axis by ANGLE2 = a from +x toward +z when ANGLE1 = 0 (Langevin et al., 2017, USGS TM 6-A55), so the tensor reads in the plane

\[K_{xx}=K_{11}\cos^2 a+K_{33}\sin^2 a,\quad K_{zz}=K_{11}\sin^2 a+K_{33}\cos^2 a,\quad K_{xz}=\left(K_{11}-K_{33}\right)\sin a\cos a\]

Far from the ends no water crosses the top and the bottom, so the exact head is a plane with

\[\frac{\partial h/\partial z}{\partial h/\partial x}=-\frac{K_{xz}}{K_{zz}},\qquad Q=\frac{K_{11}K_{33}}{K_{zz}}\left(-\frac{\partial h}{\partial x}\right)w\,D\]

where \(Q\) is the flow along the section, \(w\) its width and \(D\) its thickness.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

The flow sets K, Kv (K33) and ANGLE2 through [flow.param], HydroModPy writes them to the NPF package with ANGLE1 and ANGLE3 at zero and XT3D on, and the run stores the heads of the five layers and the constant-head flows. MODFLOW 6 turns K11 from +x toward +z for a positive ANGLE2, so the head rises with elevation when the flow runs east. The opposite sign flips the vertical head gradient, and an axis error or the two-point flux without XT3D changes or removes it: each moves the heads by a share of the 0.29 m drop over the depth. The mirrored variant runs ANGLE2 = -20 deg against its own reference.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt: Twice the MODFLOW-NWT measurement with the validation profile (head closure 1e-9 m): RMSE 3.2e-7 m, max error 6.1e-7 m. The case is linear (heads above the cell top, full cell thickness), and the centered scheme gives about 4e-7 m on the 50-column grid.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with the PETSc VI engine on the 50 x 5 strip of equal-area triangles (2 m2): RMSE 4.2e-6 m, max error 4.3e-6 m, an almost uniform offset. The drain is C * max(h - z_top, 0) with the explicit conductance C = K * A / b = 5e-8 m2/s on every cell; a positive value is what lifts the upper obstacle, and a scalar per cell gives the leakance K / b only because the cells have equal areas. A column holds two triangles whose centroids sit at dx/3 and 2 dx/3; their mean exceeds the reference at the column center by u'' (dx/6)^2 / 2 = 4.1e-6 m. Against the reference averaged over the two centroids the strip reads RMSE 8.8e-8 m. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The drain moves the profile by up to 9.0e-2 m and a 10 % change of the leakance by 8.9e-3 m, three orders above the bound. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: 9e-16 m measured; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6: MODFLOW 6 stops at its default head closure of 1e-4 m, which is the whole error of this case. Twice the measurement: RMSE 1.2e-4 m, max error 1.9e-4 m. MODFLOW-NWT closes at 1e-9 m and reads 3.2e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the 352-triangle strip: RMSE 2.7e-4 m, max error 3.7e-4 m. Each drain takes C = K * cell_area / b, so the leakance K / b is the same on every triangle and the 1D reference holds on this mesh. With a head closure of 1e-7 m the strip gives an RMSE of 1.8e-4 m, and 3.6e-5 m on a mesh of 1588 triangles: the triangle error falls with the mesh, and the rest is the default MODFLOW 6 head closure of 1e-4 m, as on the grid. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Twice the error measured on the 190-node Voronoi dual of the triangle strip: RMSE 8.8e-5 m, max error 1.8e-4 m, below the triangles (2.7e-4 m and 3.7e-4 m). Each drain takes C = K * dual_cell_area / b, so the leakance K / b is the same on every dual cell and the 1D reference holds on this mesh. The heads are posed on the faces, where the cells are seeded. Each cell is read at its node and the profile is the area-weighted mean per 2 m column, for the model and the reference alike; one column holds no node and is filled by index. What is left is the default MODFLOW 6 head closure of 1e-4 m, as on the triangles. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: head_profile.rmse 1.8e-4 (measure 8.78e-5, default head closure of 1e-4 m); head_profile.max_abs_error 3.6e-4 (measure 1.8e-4, default head closure of 1e-4 m).

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

Same closed form as the kernel-level unit test (tests/unit/model/soil/test_kernel.py), but reached the way a run reaches it: through compute_soil_forcings, with a single SAFRAN cell's precipitation and ETP passed in as FieldRecord and the recharge read back from the FieldRecord it returns.

spinup = "none" starts the soil full - "the state of a soil in a wet winter", its own description says - which is exactly the soil a year of rain has already filled. Section 7 gives the closed form for a pulse landing on that full soil and then routed through a linear reservoir of time constant k: Q(0) = 50(1 - k a), Q(t>=1) = 50 k a^2 exp(-(t-1)/k) with a = 1 - exp(-1/k). t95, the day the cumulative recharge first reaches 95 % of the 50 mm pulse, follows the continuous crossing -k ln(0.05) within the one day the discretization can miss it by.

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 82: Soil transit store impulse volume, |sum_t Q - 50| over 60 k days, mm: 1e-12 (Machine epsilon. The tail beyond 60 k days holds 50 exp(-60), below 1e-24 mm)
  • Row 86: Routed impulse validation case, t95 against -k ln 0.05, days: 1 (Discretisation. Daily steps: the cumulative recharge crosses 95 % within the day that follows the continuous crossing)

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of boussinesq: PETSc TS VI, the boussinesq variant. The onset is read on 10-day periods and the contact on 10 m columns, so both errors move in steps: measured 10 days and 10 m, one step each, and the bounds sit half a step above. The trajectory RMSE, 5.0 m, keeps its previous bound of 9 m, 1.8 times the measurement. Reversal and clearance are solver-closure bounds. Row spread: 9e-16 m measured, bound 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: The default local engine, regularized partition closure, one backward-Euler step a period. The onset is read on 10-day periods and the contact on 10 m columns: measured 20 days (two periods, PETSc reads one) and 10 m, and the bounds sit half a step above. Trajectory RMSE twice the measured 5.77 m (6.45 m until 2026-10-10, when the release followed the saturated share of the cell). Reversal and clearance are solver-closure bounds. Row spread: 8e-9 m measured, bound 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6: MODFLOW 6, same model as MODFLOW-NWT (40 x 3 cells of 10 m, 12 periods of 10 days, DRN at the land surface with b = 1 m), IMS closed at 1e-8 m. The front sits on the reference column at every period: onset error 0 d, trajectory error 0 m, so the bounds sit half a step above, 5 d and 5 m, and fail on any miss (a miss reads 10 m, RMSE 2.9 m). The closest the contact test comes to its threshold is 1.6e-3 m. The head stays below the surface for the 120 days, so the DRN never acts: the largest clearance is 0 on the held cell. Reversal is a solver-closure bound. Row spread: 3.7e-9 m measured, bound 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: MODFLOW 6 on 586 irregular triangles of about 6 m (DISV), 12 periods of 10 days, DRN at the land surface with b = 1 m. The surface is 5.0 m at the mean centroid of the two boundary triangles of the east face (x = 398.29 m), where the reference poses its outlet, and comes from a 2.5 m raster. Model and reference are averaged over the same 10 m bins, weighted by triangle area. The onset is one period late (50 d against 40 d): at x = 385 m and 40 d the reference sits 0.2 mm inside the 7.5 cm contact threshold and the model 1.7 mm below it, so the column turns one step later. The front is one column behind at 40 d and ahead at 120 d: trajectory RMSE 4.1 m, max 10 m. The bounds sit half a step above the onset and max and twice the RMSE. The head stays below the surface for the 120 days (largest clearance -2.8e-3 m), so the DRN never acts. Reversal is a solver-closure bound. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: MODFLOW 6 on the 315-node Voronoi dual of the same triangles, 12 periods of 10 days, DRN at the land surface with b = 1 m. The surface is 5.0 m on the nodes of the east face (x = 400 m), from a 2.5 m raster. Each cell is read at its node and the profile is the area-weighted mean per 10 m column, for the model and the reference alike. The onset is one period early (50 d against 60 d: the reference reads 2.6e-4 m from its own contact threshold), so the front is one column ahead at 3 of 12 periods (50, 80 and 120 d): onset error 10 d, trajectory RMSE 5.0 m, max 10 m. The bounds sit half a step above the onset and max and twice the RMSE. The head stays below the surface for the 120 days (largest clearance -2.8e-3 m), so the DRN never acts. Reversal is a solver-closure bound. The row spread is zero by construction. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: uniformity.row_spread 1e-9 (measure 8.88e-16, float rounding of the area-weighted mean).
  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt: MODFLOW-NWT, 40 x 3 cells of 10 m, 12 periods of 10 days, the land surface a DRN of conductance K * area / b with b = 1 m. The surface is 5.0 m, the outlet head, at the center of the last column (x = 395 m, where the model holds the head), and the reference is the linearized response with its outlet there. The onset is read on 10-day periods and the contact on 10 m columns with a 7.5 cm tolerance: the front sits on the reference column at every period (onset error 0 d, trajectory error 0 m), so the bounds sit half a step above, 5 d and 5 m, and fail on any miss (a miss reads 10 m, RMSE 2.9 m). The closest the contact test comes to its threshold is 1.6e-3 m. The head stays below the surface for the 120 days, so the DRN never acts: the largest clearance is 0 on the held cell. Where it acts the head stands above the surface by (R + K S^2) b / K = 3.9e-4 m (measured on the steady case), so the 1e-6 m bound fails a run in which the water table reaches the surface. Reversal is a solver-closure bound. Row spread is zero by construction of the rows.

Thin-aquifer Brutsaert recession benchmark#

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: nonlinear late recession of Brutsaert and Nieber (1977) for a strip drained on one side, Q(t) = (Q*^(-1/2) + a t / 2)^(-2).

\[-\frac{dQ}{dt}=a\,Q^{3/2},\qquad Q(t)=\left(Q_*^{-1/2}+\frac{a\,t}{2}\right)^{-2},\qquad a=\frac{C\,\sqrt{K}\,W}{S_y\,(B\,W)^{3/2}}\]

\(K\) is the hydraulic conductivity, \(S_y\) the specific yield, \(B\) the drainage length, \(W\) the outlet width and \(C = 3\,I^{3/2} = 2.4025\) with \(I=\int_0^1 p\,(1-p^3)^{-1/2}\,dp\). Twice \(C\) is the 4.804 of Brutsaert and Nieber (1977), written for a channel drained from both banks (validation_cases/analytical/transient/brutsaert_reference.py).

Deep-aquifer Brutsaert recession benchmark#

pass, known gap end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Known gap: modflow6_voronoi

Known gap. The fitted decay rate is 0.66 % under the linearized law, 0.22 % on the triangles. Backward Euler explains 0.33 % at 100 steps a period (0.09 % at 400, as on the structured grid, which has no space error). The rest, 0.32 % at 400 steps, is spatial. The lowest eigenvalue of the dual operator, assembled from the stored cell polygons (K D L / d between nodes, Sy times the polygon area, the 3 outlet nodes held, no time stepping), is 0.346 % under pi^2 K D / (4 Sy B^2) with B = 400 m. With B = 400.69 m, the length that eigenvalue implies, the same run reads -0.318 % on the rate and 0.52 % on the late RMSE, the time-stepping values. The mesh is irregular and its outlet face holds 3 nodes, 15 m apart; a finer bundle was not built.

Compared with: linearized Boussinesq recession of a deep strip after steady recharge, whose tail is the exponential law of Brutsaert and Nieber (1977).

\[Q(t)=Q_0\,\frac{B}{B-d}\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{8\cos\!\left(\frac{k\pi d}{2B}\right)}{k^2\pi^2}\,e^{-k^2 a t},\qquad k=2n-1,\qquad a=\frac{\pi^2\,K\,D}{4\,S_y\,B^2}\]

\(Q_0\) is the steady discharge at the end of the warm-up, \(K\) the hydraulic conductivity, \(S_y\) the specific yield, \(D\) the saturated thickness at the outlet, \(B\) the drainage length and \(d\) the length near the outlet that the model does not recharge. The first term alone is the late exponential law (validation_cases/analytical/transient/brutsaert_reference.py).

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6, modflow6_irregular_tri: The run stores the mean discharge of each 10-day period, over its 100 backward-Euler steps, and the reference is the mean of the series solution over the same period. Twice the measured error: relative RMSE 8.4e-4 to 9.3e-4, maximum 2.2e-3 to 2.4e-3, on the first period, where the fast modes decay within a few steps. The maximum falls with the step, 6.4e-3, 2.2e-3 and 1.15e-3 at 25, 100 and 400 steps a period on MODFLOW 6, down to a floor of 1.1e-3 on the first two periods that a 5 m grid leaves where it is. Until 2026-10-10 the run stored the discharge of the last step of each period and the reference was read at the period end: RMSE 1.3e-4, maximum 2e-4.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: The band of tolerances.toml, shared with MODFLOW. The PETSc runtime takes the 100 backward-Euler steps a period of the case, as MODFLOW does, stores the mean discharge of each period and reads relative RMSE 8.4e-4, maximum 2.2e-3 against the period means of the series solution, decay rate -0.31 %, |b - 1| 2.7e-4 and late RMSE 0.0054, against 8.4e-4 to 9.0e-4, 2.2e-3 to 2.3e-3, -0.32 to -0.34 %, 2.7e-4 to 4.7e-4 and 0.0057 to 0.0061 for MODFLOW on the grid. With 4 steps a period (before 2026-10-09) the rate came out 7.6 % low.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: The band of tolerances.toml, shared with MODFLOW. The default 'auto' engine runs local on these 240 cells and takes the 100 backward-Euler steps a period of the case, as MODFLOW does, and stores the mean discharge of each period. With the Newton closure of the case (1e-12 m3/s, see config_boussinesq_local.toml) it reads relative RMSE 8.4e-4, maximum 2.2e-3 against the period means of the series solution, decay rate -0.31 %, |b - 1| 2.7e-4 and late RMSE 0.0054, the PETSc values to three digits, against 8.4e-4 to 9.0e-4, 2.2e-3 to 2.3e-3, -0.32 to -0.34 %, 2.7e-4 to 4.7e-4 and 0.0057 to 0.0061 for MODFLOW on the grid. Before 2026-10-09 this engine took one step a period whatever the case asked.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: The outlet nodes lie on the east edge, so the drainage length is the full 400 m. Measured on the 321-node dual: discharge RMSE 4.4e-4 and maximum 6.9e-4 (twice that), rate error -0.663 % and late RMSE 1.955 % (1.1 times, with the gap), exponent error 3.5e-4 (twice that). The run is deterministic: a relative perturbation of K by 1e-12 to 5e-12 moves the rate error by less than 1e-11. The dual keeps the ILUT fill of 40 of the triangle config, which stops the linear solver from stalling on this matrix. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader bins the dual by node abscissa into one profile (7e-15 m measured). B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Tightened to twice the measure: recession.exponent_abs_error 7e-4 to 6.99e-4 (measure 3.49e-4); discharge.relative_rmse 9e-4 to 8.76e-4 (measure 4.38e-4); discharge.relative_max_error 0.0014 to 0.00139 (measure 6.92e-4). Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: uniformity.row_spread 1e-9 (measure 7.11e-15, float rounding of the area-weighted mean).

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

The reference of the two Brutsaert cases is a closed form. This test solves the Boussinesq equation of the strip on a fine finite-volume grid with SciPy, from the same steady water table under recharge, and asks the closed forms to match it. It pins the constant of the nonlinear law for a strip drained on one side and the modal weights of the linear series, without running a solver.

Test functions

  • Nonlinear law matches a fine dupuit strip drained on one side.
  • Linear series matches a fine deep strip with an unrecharged outlet strip.

MODFLOW 6 GWT first-order decay against its closed form#

pass modflow6

Not run on

  • NWT: MODFLOW-NWT has no GWT. HydroModPy transports on NWT with MT3DMS, a separate code whose decay rate is in 1/day, so the per-second GWT clock this file guards does not exist there.
  • MF6 triangles, MF6 Voronoi: The case is one closed cell with no flow, advection or dispersion, so its result cannot depend on the mesh. A triangle or Voronoi DISV would repeat the same cell.
  • Boussinesq, Boussinesq default: The Boussinesq solver has no transport: the registry holds no transport adapter for it and the solver page lists its transport as refused. This file runs MODFLOW 6 GWT.

Compared with: the first-order decay C(t) = C0 exp(-k t) of a closed cell.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

With no advection and no dispersion, a uniform initial concentration decays as C(t) = C0 * exp(-k t) under the MF6 MST first-order decay term. The MF6 GWT clock is SECONDS, so the decay rate k is in 1/s. This guards the per-second unit contract for transport.modflow6gwt.parameters.rate_decay: a per-day value would be ~86400x too large and annihilate the solute.

Tolerance rationale - tests/TOLERANCES.md row 35: max relative concentration error < 1 % (decay is exact in MST; the allowance covers finite time-stepping).

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 35: MF6 GWT first-order decay 0D, max relative concentration error vs C0*exp(-k t): < 1 % (First-order decay is exact in MF6 MST with no advection or dispersion; small allowance for finite time-stepping)

Growth of a groundwater mound under a rectangle of recharge against Hantush (1967)#

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: Hantush (1967) mound under a rectangle of uniform recharge, linearized with the mean saturated thickness b = (hi + hm(t)) / 2 taken at the center hm, solved at each time; S* integrated with scipy.integrate.quad_vec. Carleton (2010, USGS SIR 2010-5102) gives the same form.

\[h^2-h_i^2=\frac{w}{2K}\,\nu t\left[S^*\!\left((l+x)n,(a+y)n\right)+S^*\!\left((l+x)n,(a-y)n\right)+S^*\!\left((l-x)n,(a+y)n\right)+S^*\!\left((l-x)n,(a-y)n\right)\right]\]
\[S^*(\alpha,\beta)=\int_0^1\operatorname{erf}\left(\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{\tau}}\right)\operatorname{erf}\left(\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{\tau}}\right)d\tau,\qquad \nu=\frac{K\bar b}{S_y},\qquad n=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\nu t}},\qquad \bar b=\frac{h_i+h_m(t)}{2}\]

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured against the Hantush mound on the 101 x 101 grid of 20 m with steps of 6 h, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: transect space-time RMSE 1.6e-3 m, max error 4.8e-3 m (the center at day 3), final transect RMSE 1.3e-3 m, final map max 5.4e-3 m, for a mound of 0.75 m. Refined with MODFLOW 6, steps of 3 and 1 h read RMSE 9.5e-4 and 9.1e-4 m on 20 m cells, the floor of the 20 m grid; cells of 6.7 m read 2.0e-3 m with 6 h steps and 4.2e-4 m with 1 h steps (max 1.2e-3 m). That limit is the linearization: a nonlinear finite-difference solution on 6.7 m cells and 45 min steps reads 3.5e-4 m and 1.1e-3 m against the reference.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc TS VI (4 backward-Euler steps a period) on the conforming triangles of the MODFLOW 6 triangle grid: transect space-time RMSE 1.1e-3 m, max error 4.7e-3 m, center max 2.2e-3 m, final transect RMSE 1.8e-3 m, final map max 9.0e-3 m. The map max sits in the cells where MODFLOW 6 reads its own on these triangles, 20 to 40 m outside the long sides of the rectangle.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine, which runs scipy_sparse on these 6806 conforming triangles with one backward-Euler step a period: transect space-time RMSE 1.37e-3 m, max error 4.6e-3 m, center max 4.4e-3 m, final transect RMSE 1.2e-3 m, final map max 1.04e-2 m. MODFLOW 6 on the same triangles reads the same within 4 %, and its refinement converges to Hantush: the error is the mesh and the step. The run stores the whole recharge, 0.99999999 of the recharged volume. Until 2026-10-10 the surface closure released 3.6 % of the recharge with the water table 10 m under the top, and the mound ended 1.7 cm low.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the conforming triangles, 6806 cells of 10 m under the rectangle and up to 80 m at the sides, whose edges follow the rectangle so each triangle takes all or none of the recharge: transect space-time RMSE 1.4e-3 m, max error 4.7e-3 m, center max 4.6e-3 m, final transect RMSE 1.2e-3 m. The final map max, 1.0e-2 m, sits 20 to 40 m outside the long sides, where triangles of 12 m meet the recharge edge: the two-point flux between centroids is not consistent on a general triangle, and the Boussinesq runtime on the same triangles reads the same cells.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Twice the error measured on the Voronoi dual, 3556 cells centered on nodes that face each other across the rectangle edges, so each cell takes all or none of the recharge: transect space-time RMSE 2.0e-3 m, max error 5.3e-3 m (the center at day 3.75), final transect RMSE 2.0e-3 m, final map max 4.5e-3 m. The dual is K-orthogonal: its map error stays at the level of the structured grid. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Tightened to twice the measure: final_time.rmse 0.0041 to 0.00404 (measure 0.00202); space_time.rmse 0.004 to 0.00399 (measure 0.00199). Already at twice the measure: final_time.map_max_abs_error 0.009 (measure 0.0045).
