Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured against the Theis drawdown, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: space-time RMSE 4.4e-3 m, max error 9.8e-3 m, final RMSE 5.3e-3 m. The azimuthal spread bound is ten times the MODFLOW 6 head closure, 1e-6 m: the grid is symmetric about the well. Until 2026-10-09 the reference evaluated E1 by an asymptotic series that is wrong between u = 1 and 8, which doubled the space-time error at the outer monitor points.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: About twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine, which runs scipy_sparse on the 10082 triangles of 71 x 71 squares (397 m2, the cell area of the MODFLOW grid) with one backward-Euler step a period: space-time RMSE 0.0048 m, max error 0.0140 m, final RMSE 0.0035 m, final max error 0.0045 m, azimuthal spread 0.0012 m. MODFLOW on its 101 x 101 grid, with the same single step a period, reads a space-time RMSE of 0.0044 m: the error is the time step and the fixed-transmissivity Theis reference. The reference is read at the centroid of the triangle each monitor point reads, with the well at the centroid of the triangle that holds it, 6.6 m off the well point. Read from the well point, that offset alone gave an azimuthal spread of 0.136 m on the former 31 x 31 mesh. Until 2026-10-10 the surface closure sent up to 3.4 m3/day of the pumping out of the well cell, 10 m under the top: space-time RMSE 0.0043 m, final max error 0.0064 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the refined triangle mesh: space-time RMSE 4.4e-3 m, max error 1.45e-2 m, final RMSE 3.4e-3 m, final max error 5.0e-3 m, azimuthal spread 0.020 m. The reference is read at the centroid of the triangle each monitor point reads, with the well at the centroid of the triangle that holds it. The well point is a mesh node, and MODFLOW 6 puts the well in the first triangle that holds it, whose centroid lies 15.4 m away: read from the well point, that offset gave an azimuthal spread of 0.087 m. The spread left, 0.020 m at 60 m where the drawdown is 0.85 m, is the asymmetry of the gmsh refinement (165 to 221 triangles per quadrant within 300 m).
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Twice the error measured on the Voronoi dual of the refined mesh, the reference read at the node of the cell each monitor point reads: space-time RMSE 9.4e-3 m, max error 2.3e-2 m, final RMSE 6.3e-3 m, final max error 7.7e-3 m, azimuthal spread of the error 2.2e-3 m. A node sits on the well, so the cell that holds the well is centered on it. Read at the monitor radius instead, 1 to 18 m from that node, the error was twice as large. Until 2026-10-10 the spread was taken on the drawdown, not on the error, and read 0.040 m: the cells read sit at different radii. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Tightened to twice the measure: space_time.azimuthal_spread 0.0044 to 0.00435 (measure 0.00217); final_time.rmse 0.013 to 0.0126 (measure 0.00625); final_time.max_abs_error 0.016 to 0.0154 (measure 0.00766); space_time.rmse 0.019 to 0.0189 (measure 0.00941); space_time.max_abs_error 0.046 to 0.0454 (measure 0.0227).

Compared with: Ferris (1951) tidal propagation into a semi-infinite linearized unconfined aquifer, T = K b with the saturated thickness b, S = Sy.

\[S_y\frac{\partial h}{\partial t}=T\frac{\partial^2 h}{\partial x^2},\qquad h(0,t)=h_0+A\cos\left(\frac{2\pi t}{t_0}\right)\]
\[h(x,t)=h_0+A\,e^{-x/\lambda}\cos\left(\frac{2\pi t}{t_0}-\frac{x}{\lambda}\right),\qquad \lambda=\sqrt{\frac{t_0\,T}{\pi\,S_y}}\]

Measured on 2026-10-13, commit 7c78961c6 with uncommitted changes, version 2.0.0a5, a local run. The last column gives the measured value and the threshold as shares of the head range of the reference over space and time, 0.46 to 0.5 m.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 50-column grid of 2 m over the last four tides, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: space-time RMSE 5.3e-3 m, max error 3.3e-2 m, final RMSE 3.4e-3 m, final max 1.0e-2 m; decay length 11.03 m and lag length 12.63 m against 11.73 m, errors of 6.0 % and 7.7 %. The error is backward Euler with one step per hourly period, 24 a tide: theory shortens the decay length and stretches the lag length by about w dt / 4 = 6.5 %. Periods of 4, 2 and 1 h give a space-time RMSE of 2.0e-2, 1.0e-2 and 5.3e-3 m, and lag-length errors of 45, 17 and 7.7 %; 16 sub-steps a period bring the decay and lag errors to 0.9 and 1.7 %, and 100 columns change the RMSE by 5 %. The max error sits in the sea column, which holds the mean tide of each hour while the reference holds the tide at the output time: A w dt / 2 = 3.3e-2 m. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc on 50 x 5 square cells of 2 m split into triangles: space-time RMSE 3.5e-3 m, max error 2.9e-2 m, final RMSE 1.1e-3 m, final max 2.8e-3 m; decay and lag length errors 1.9 and 2.5 %. PETSc takes 4 backward-Euler steps a period (TS VI), and MODFLOW 6 with 4 sub-steps a period reads 2.0 and 2.8 % on the same tide, so the error is first order in time. The max error sits in the sea column, which holds the mean tide of each hour. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads 1e-15 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: Twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine, which runs scipy_sparse on these 500 triangles with one backward-Euler step a period: space-time RMSE 5.1e-3 m, max error 3.1e-2 m, final RMSE 3.4e-3 m, final max 1.0e-2 m; decay and lag length errors 5.9 and 7.5 %, the MODFLOW values of tolerances.toml, where the error is explained. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the sparse engine reads 4e-11 m; the bound is 1e-7 m, as on the sibling strips.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the triangle strip of 1446 cells about 1.5 m across, the sea head posed at the mean centroid of the triangles on the west face: space-time RMSE 4.9e-3 m, max error 2.9e-2 m, final RMSE 3.5e-3 m, final max 1.0e-2 m; decay and lag length errors 6.0 and 7.1 %. As on the structured grid, the error is backward Euler with one step per hourly period (see tolerances.toml). The row spread is zero by construction: the loader collapses the strip to one profile.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Twice the error measured on the Voronoi dual of the triangle strip, 763 cells centered on the nodes, the sea head held on the nodes of the west face and the reference read at the node of each cell: space-time RMSE 6.4e-3 m, max error 3.6e-2 m, final RMSE 5.9e-3 m, final max 1.8e-2 m; decay and lag length errors 5.9 and 7.2 %. The decay and lag match the other grids, so the error is backward Euler with one step per hourly period (see tolerances.toml); the dual cells are twice as large as the triangles, which adds to the RMSE. The row spread is zero by construction: the comparison bins the cells into one profile. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Tightened to twice the measure: tide.decay_length_relative_error 0.12 to 0.119 (measure 0.0592); final_profile.rmse 0.012 to 0.0118 (measure 0.00589); final_profile.max_abs_error 0.037 to 0.0366 (measure 0.0183); space_time.rmse 0.013 to 0.0129 (measure 0.00643); space_time.max_abs_error 0.073 to 0.0728 (measure 0.0364).

Schedule. modflow_nwt, modflow6, modflow6_irregular_tri, modflow6_voronoi, boussinesq_local: runs in Nightly / validation no PETSc, Weekly / Cross Platform, Tests / fast marker. boussinesq: runs in Nightly / validation PETSc (skipped in Tests / fast marker: no petsc4py there). Jobs.

Linearized unconfined transient cases against their analytical references#

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_localpetsc_ts_vi_obstaclepetsc_vi_obstacle

Compared with: linearized 1D unconfined response to a piecewise west-boundary series; linearized 1D unconfined response to a step of the west boundary head; linearized 1D unconfined response to a sinusoidal recharge; linearized 1D unconfined response to a recharge step; linearized 1D unconfined response to a recharge step in a deep aquifer, where the linearization error is smaller.

Case lu_boundary_piecewise_1d

\[S_y\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}=T_0\frac{\partial^2 \eta}{\partial x^2},\qquad \eta(L,t)=0\]
\[\eta(x,t)=\sum_k \Delta h_k\,\eta_{\mathrm{step}}(x,t-t_k)\,H(t-t_k)\]

Case lu_boundary_step_1d

\[S_y\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}=T_0\frac{\partial^2 \eta}{\partial x^2},\qquad \eta(0,t)=\Delta h\,H(t),\qquad \eta(L,t)=0\]
\[\eta(x,t)=\Delta h\left[1-\frac{x}{L}-\frac{2}{\pi}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\sin\left(n\pi x/L\right)}{n}\exp\left(-D\left(n\pi/L\right)^2 t\right)\right]\]

Case lu_recharge_periodic_1d

\[S_y\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}=T_0\frac{\partial^2 \eta}{\partial x^2}+R(t),\qquad h=h_0+\eta\]
\[R(t)=\overline{R}+A\sin\left(2\pi t/P+\phi\right)\]

Case lu_recharge_step_1d

\[S_y\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}=T_0\frac{\partial^2 \eta}{\partial x^2}+R_0\,H(t),\qquad h=h_0+\eta\]
\[\eta(x,t)=\frac{R_0}{2T_0}x(L-x)-\frac{4R_0L^2}{T_0\pi^3}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{\sin\left((2n+1)\pi x/L\right)}{(2n+1)^3}\exp\left(-D\left((2n+1)\pi/L\right)^2 t\right)\]

Case lu_recharge_step_deep_1d

\[S_y\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t}=T_0\frac{\partial^2 \eta}{\partial x^2}+R_0\,H(t),\qquad h=h_0+\eta\]
\[T_0=K\,h_{\mathrm{ref}},\qquad D=\frac{T_0}{S_y}\]

Measured on 2026-10-13, commit 7c78961c6 with uncommitted changes, version 2.0.0a5, a local run. The last column gives the measured value and the threshold as shares of the head range of the reference over space and time, 0.0137 to 0.3 m.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6, petsc_ts_vi_obstacle, petsc_vi_obstacle: Twice the error measured on the 50-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: space-time RMSE 6.1e-3 m, max error 3.3e-2 m, final RMSE 2.8e-3 m. Backward Euler is first order in time: on the boundary step, 1, 2, 4 and 8 sub-steps per period give a space-time RMSE of 1.4e-3, 7.1e-4, 3.4e-4 and 1.6e-4 m. The heads are posed at the centers of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc on 50 x 5 square cells of 2 m: space-time RMSE 0.0016 m, max error 0.0082 m, final RMSE 0.00071 m. PETSc takes 4 backward-Euler steps a period (TS VI); the error is first order in time, so it sits below the one-step MODFLOW band of this case. The heads sit dx/3 inside the faces. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: The band of tolerances.toml, shared with MODFLOW. On this 500-cell strip the default 'auto' engine runs scipy_sparse, one backward-Euler step a period as MODFLOW does, and on 50 x 5 square cells of 2 m it reads space-time RMSE 0.0061 m, max error 0.033 m, final RMSE 0.0027 m, against 6.1e-3, 3.3e-2 and 2.8e-3 m for MODFLOW. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the sparse engine reads 3e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Twice the error measured on the triangle strip: space-time RMSE 6.1e-3 m, max error 3.3e-2 m, final RMSE 2.9e-3 m. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader collapses the strip to one profile. Backward Euler is first order in time: on the boundary step, 1, 2, 4 and 8 sub-steps per period give a space-time RMSE of 1.4e-3, 7.1e-4, 3.4e-4 and 1.6e-4 m. The heads are posed at the centers of the boundary cells.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Twice the error measured on the 190-node Voronoi dual of the triangle strip: space-time RMSE 6.11e-3 m, max error 3.35e-2 m, final RMSE 2.91e-3 m, final max error 4.14e-3 m. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader collapses the dual to one profile, binned by node abscissa with polygon-area weights. Backward Euler is first order in time: on the Voronoi dual of the boundary step, 1, 4 and 8 sub-steps per period give a space-time RMSE of 1.4e-3, 3.7e-4 and 1.8e-4 m. The side heads sit on the faces, where the cells are seeded.
  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 50-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: space-time RMSE 1.4e-3 m, max error 1.2e-2 m, final RMSE 9.0e-5 m. Backward Euler is first order in time: on the boundary step, 1, 2, 4 and 8 sub-steps per period give a space-time RMSE of 1.4e-3, 7.1e-4, 3.4e-4 and 1.6e-4 m. The heads are posed at the centers of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc on 40 x 4 square cells of 2.5 m: space-time RMSE 0.00034 m, max error 0.0032 m, final RMSE 7.3e-05 m. PETSc takes 4 backward-Euler steps a period (TS VI); the error is first order in time, so it sits below the one-step MODFLOW band of this case. The heads sit dx/3 inside the faces. What the test does, all thresholds, the file

This driver folds five sibling 1D linearized-unconfined transient benchmarks into one parametrized suite. Each scenario keeps its own forcing (via its own launcher comparison function) and its own tolerances (read from the per-case tolerance TOML through the comparison payload). The references pose the side heads where the model holds them, at the centers of the boundary cells.

Case lu_boundary_piecewise_1d: Linearized Unconfined Boundary Piecewise 1D

Run it alone: python -m validation_cases.analytical.transient.linearized_unconfined_boundary_piecewise_1d.run_case

Run it alone: python -m validation_cases.analytical.transient.linearized_unconfined_recharge_periodic_1d.run_case

pass modflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoi

Not run on

  • NWT: MODFLOW-NWT has no PRT. HydroModPy tracks particles on NWT with MODPATH 6, a separate code with its own input; this file runs the MODFLOW 6 PRT package.
  • Boussinesq, Boussinesq default: The Boussinesq solver has no particle tracking: the registry holds no transport adapter for it and the solver page lists its transport as refused. This file runs MODFLOW 6 PRT.

Compared with: the straight particle path x(t) = x0 + v t in a uniform flow, v = q / porosity.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

For a constant-gradient (uniform) flow field, Pollock's method is exact, so a particle moves as x(t) = x0 + v*t with v = q / porosity (q is the specific discharge). The pore velocity v is read back from the model's DATA-SPDIS instead of being hard-coded, then the track positions are checked against the analytical streamline.

Three grids run the same strip. modflow6 is a rectilinear DIS column. modflow6_irregular_tri and modflow6_voronoi are DISV strips of jittered triangles and Voronoi polygons (tests/validation/helpers/disv_meshes.py), the topology HydroModPy always gives PRT. The end cells hold the exact linear head at their centers, so the flow is uniform for any mesh whose flux is consistent. The triangle strip has a p95 connection non-orthogonality of 40 deg, above the 30 deg trigger, so HydroModPy's rule switches XT3D on and the test runs with it; the Voronoi strip is orthogonal and runs with the two-point flux.

Control run on the same triangles with the two-point flux (XT3D off): the streamline is off by 17 %, so the non-orthogonal flux, not the tracking, is what XT3D repairs. Measured here with XT3D as the rule decides: triangles 2.5e-4, Voronoi 2.6e-6, DIS 1e-15.

Tolerance rationale - tests/TOLERANCES.md row 34: max relative position error < 1 % (Pollock is exact for uniform velocity; the allowance covers cell-crossing arithmetic). The same row holds for the DISV strips, where the polygons are split into sub-cells for tracking. The transverse drift of the particle is held to the same bound.

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 34: MF6 PRT uniform-velocity streamline, max relative position error |x-x_exp|/|x_exp-x0|: < 1 % (Pollock's method is exact for a uniform velocity field; small allowance for cell-crossing arithmetic)

Test functions

Stream depletion of a well pumping beside a stream held at a fixed head#

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: Glover and Balmer (1954) stream depletion and the image-well Theis drawdown (Theis 1941), with T = K b and S = Sy, read at the stream, well and monitor cell centers.

\[\frac{Q_s}{Q}=\operatorname{erfc}\left(\sqrt{\frac{S a^2}{4 T t}}\right)\]
\[s(x,y,t)=\frac{Q}{4\pi T}\left[E_1\left(\frac{r_1^2 S}{4 T t}\right)-E_1\left(\frac{r_2^2 S}{4 T t}\right)\right]\]
\[T=K\,b,\qquad S=S_y\]

a is the distance from the well to the stream, r1 the distance to the well and r2 the distance to its image across the stream.

Measured on 2026-10-13, commit 7c78961c6 with uncommitted changes, version 2.0.0a5, a local run. The last column gives the measured value and the threshold as shares of the largest drawdown of the reference, 0.308 to 0.323 m.

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike to 1e-5: stream depletion 0.0142 at most, on the first half day, and 0.00034 at day 20; drawdown space-time RMSE 1.6e-3 m, max 6.4e-3 m, final RMSE 1.7e-3 m, final max 3.6e-3 m. The run stores the mean depletion of each period, over its 4 backward-Euler steps, and the reference is the mean of the closed form over the same period. The depletion error is the backward-Euler step: on MODFLOW 6 it falls to 0.0076, 0.0042 and 0.0024 with 8, 16 and 32 steps a period, and moves by 1e-4 on a 5 m grid. Until 2026-10-10 the run stored the depletion of the last step and the reference was read at the period end: 0.0083 at most. The drawdown error is the grid and the unconfined flow: on a 5 m grid the RMSE halves, and at a tenth of the pumping rate the final error near the well falls from 3.6e-3 to 2.2e-4 m, the s^2 / (2 b) of the water table. The closed sides do not count: on a domain 1.5 times wider and longer the results move by 6e-6. Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of modflow_nwt, modflow6: Twice the error measured on the 50-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: space-time RMSE 1.4e-3 m, max error 1.2e-2 m, final RMSE 9.0e-5 m. Backward Euler is first order in time: on the boundary step, 1, 2, 4 and 8 sub-steps per period give a space-time RMSE of 1.4e-3, 7.1e-4, 3.4e-4 and 1.6e-4 m. The heads are posed at the centers of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
  • Thresholds of boussinesq: Twice the error measured with PETSc on 40 x 4 square cells of 2.5 m: space-time RMSE 0.00034 m, max error 0.0032 m, final RMSE 7.3e-05 m. PETSc takes 4 backward-Euler steps a period (TS VI); the error is first order in time, so it sits below the one-step MODFLOW band of this case. The heads sit dx/3 inside the faces. Before 2026-10-09 the 40-column strips had 3 rows, cells of 2.5 x 3.3 m: on right triangles of unequal sides the two-point flux of the solver is not consistent, and the recharge step ended 1.1e-2 m off. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: The band of tolerances.toml, shared with MODFLOW. The default local engine takes one backward-Euler step a period, as MODFLOW does, and on 40 x 4 square cells of 2.5 m it reads space-time RMSE 0.0014 m, max error 0.012 m, final RMSE 9.9e-05 m, against 1.4e-3, 1.2e-2 and 9.0e-5 m for MODFLOW. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A stress period holds a constant forcing, and HydroModPy stores only its end state. Against the closed form of a step at a Dirichlet boundary, h(x, t) = dh * erfc(x / (2 sqrt(D t))) with D = K b / S, this case pins three statements that are easy to get backwards:

1. simulation.time.substeps_per_period is the knob. The default of one backward-Euler step over the whole period carries an order of magnitude more error than ten. 2. A geometric partition (MODFLOW TSMULT) cannot help. Within a period the forcing is constant, so the backward-Euler end state is a commuting product over the steps: it depends on the multiset of step sizes and not on their order, and equal steps minimize its error. A growth ratio and its reciprocal give the same error, both worse than equal steps. This is why HydroModPy declares TSMULT = 1 and exposes no growth field. 3. Adaptive time stepping must not undo the request. MF6 ignores the TDIS NSTP of a period ATS covers, so the ATS record has to carry the declared step as both its starting and its maximum value.

A fourth test leaves the closed form for HydroModPy's own configuration, a seasonal recharge on a hillslope drained by surface DRN cells and a river. There the default of one step per period is not a small bias: it moves the monthly discharge, the quantity a calibration scores against, by tens of percent. The default is left at 1 because the right count is a property of the model (tau = L**2 S / (K b) against the period length) and the cost is linear in it, but a run that leaves it there is making a choice, not accepting a neutral value.

The first, second and fourth tests run on MODFLOW 6 and on MODFLOW-NWT, both built straight in flopy: NWT is backward Euler with TSMULT as well, and the rows 65, 66 and 68 hold for it unchanged. The third test is MODFLOW 6 only, as MODFLOW-NWT has no adaptive time stepping. The fifth test runs the Boussinesq solver, PETSc and default engine, through its own driver. That driver takes substeps_per_period equal backward-Euler steps per period, so statement 1 holds there; it has no growth ratio and no ATS, so statements 2 and 3 do not apply. The PETSc run sets ts_vi_steps_per_period = 1 so that the driver is the only source of sub-steps.

Tolerances: tests/TOLERANCES.md rows 65-68, and the floor of _BOUSSINESQ_RATIO_FLOOR for the fifth test.

Run it alone: python -m validation_cases.analytical.transient.linearized_unconfined_boundary_step_1d.run_case

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 65: Stress-period sub-stepping (MF6), RMSE ratio between nstp=1 and nstp=10: > 10x (Derived. Backward Euler is first order in time, so halving the step halves the error; ten steps should gain about an order of magnitude on a smooth relaxation, and the assertion is the weakest form of that (a strict factor 10) rather than a fitted ratio)
  • Row 66: Stress-period sub-stepping (MF6), RMSE difference between TSMULT r and 1/r: 1e-6 m (Derived. Within a stress period the forcing is constant, so the backward-Euler end state is a product of commuting operators over the steps: it depends on the multiset of step sizes and not on their order, and a ratio and its reciprocal only reverse that order. The identity is exact in exact arithmetic, so the band is the iterative closure, declared at DVCLOSE = 1e-3 m by COMPLEXITY SIMPLE)
  • Row 67: Adaptive time stepping (MF6), RMSE relative difference, ATS on against ATS off: 1e-12 (Machine epsilon. Nothing fails on this column, so ATS never cuts, and with dt0 = dtmax = perlen / nstp it replays the declared partition step for step. The two runs are the same arithmetic in the same order)
  • Row 68: One step per stress period (MF6), monthly discharge drift against a refined run: 0.10 (Derived. Backward Euler is first order, so the drift scales with the step; on the hillslope this case builds it is measured at 28 % with one step per month against thirty, and it stays above 10 % across the whole plausible bedrock range (K from 1e-7 to 1e-4 m/s gave 4 % to 28 %). The floor is set at 10 %, well inside the measured band, because the row exists to state that the drift is large and not to pin its exact value)
  • Row 132: Stress-period sub-stepping (Boussinesq), RMSE ratio between nstp=1 and nstp=10: > 4.8x (Derived. Backward Euler is first order, so ten steps would gain about ten on the time error alone; the strip's spatial error and the linearization of the closed form hold the ratio just under ten, so the floor is half of what is measured. Head step on a 20 x 2 strip of 5 m cells, one 12 h period, substeps_per_period read by the Boussinesq driver (tests/validation/analytical/transient/test_stress_period_substepping.py))

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A fully penetrating well pumps at constant rate Q in a confined aquifer overlain by a leaky aquitard of thickness b' and vertical conductivity K'. A source bed of constant head sits above the aquitard. Under these assumptions the analytical drawdown is the Hantush solution:

s(r, t) = Q / (4 pi T) * W(u, r / B)

with u = r^2 S / (4 T t), B = sqrt(T b' / K') the leakage factor and the Hantush well function

W(u, beta) = int_u^inf (1/y) exp(-y - beta^2 / (4 y)) dy.

The numerical reference is a three-layer MF6 IMS model:

* layer 0: source bed - all cells are CHD at the initial head,
* layer 1: aquitard - thickness ``b'`` and K = ``K'``, no storage,
* layer 2: main pumped aquifer - thickness ``b``, K such that
``T = K b``, specific storage such that ``S = S_s b``.

A telescoping grid concentrates resolution near the well; the outer Dirichlet ring sits well beyond the radius of influence ~sqrt(4 T t / S). Drawdown is compared at radii 10/50/100 m and times 1/3/10 d.

Four grids run the same sandwich, well, time steps and probes:

* ``modflow6``: the MF6 telescoping rectilinear DIS grid above.
* ``modflow_nwt``: the same grid and layers in MODFLOW-NWT (UPW, three
 confined layers, layer 0 and the outer ring of layer 2 at ``ibound = -1``,
 ``headtol = 1e-8`` m so the closure cannot hide the 2 % bound).
* ``modflow6_irregular_tri`` and ``modflow6_voronoi``: three layers on a DISV
 disc of jittered concentric rings (``tests/validation/helpers/disv_meshes.py``),
 cells growing by 1.2 per ring out to 1 km (ten leakage factors, where the
 drawdown is 3e-6 m). Layer 0 holds the head in every cell, layer 2 in the
 cells with a boundary edge, and the well pumps from the layer 2 cell that
 holds the origin. The probe is the cell whose center is the closest to the
 target point; the closed form uses the discrete distance between centers.

XT3D on the triangles follows HydroModPy's rule (DisvMesh.xt3d_reason): the triangle disc has a p95 connection non-orthogonality of 37 deg, above the 30 deg trigger, so XT3D is on (control run with the two-point flux: 1.28 % instead of 0.61 %). The Voronoi disc is orthogonal and runs with the two-point flux.

Tolerance rationale - tests/TOLERANCES.md row 6: NSE > 0.99 and maximum pointwise relative error below 2 %, for every grid. Measured maximum relative error: rectilinear 0.81 %, NWT 0.81 %, triangles 0.61 %, Voronoi 1.31 % (NSE above 0.9995 for all). The drawdown is steady from the first probe time, so the three times of a radius carry one error.

Scope - solver_sanity: The three-layer sandwich (source / aquitard / pumped aquifer) and the telescoping grid are built directly on the flopy SDK because the hydromodpy launcher TOML does not expose this geometry. The test therefore validates MODFLOW 6 against the Hantush analytical solution, not the hydromodpy pipeline. The NWT leg checks the NWT binary against the same closed form.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A semi-infinite column is initially solute-free and subjected to a constant-concentration injection c0 at x = 0 under steady uniform flow of pore velocity v with longitudinal dispersion coefficient D. The analytical solution is the Ogata-Banks profile:

c(x, t) = c0 / 2 * [ erfc((x - v t) / (2 sqrt(D t)))
                    + exp(v x / D) * erfc((x + v t) / (2 sqrt(D t))) ]

The reference is a 1D MF6 GWF + GWT model: flow is driven by a constant injection flux on the left and a CHD sink on the right producing a uniform pore velocity v; transport is solved with a constant concentration c0 at the inlet and an open boundary at the outlet. Numerical and analytical concentrations are compared at probe points along the column at three times.

Three grids run the same column. modflow6 is the rectilinear DIS column above. modflow6_irregular_tri and modflow6_voronoi are DISV strips three cells wide of jittered triangles and Voronoi polygons (tests/validation/helpers/disv_meshes.py), the topology HydroModPy always gives GWT. There the end cells hold the exact linear head h(x) = i (L - x) at their centers (pore velocity v for any consistent flux), the inlet cells hold the concentration c0, and the closed form starts at the mean center of those cells. A probe averages the cells whose center lies within half a cell of x, and the closed form is averaged over the same centers. Dispersion keeps MODFLOW 6's default XT3D, as HydroModPy's GWT does. The flow follows HydroModPy's XT3D rule (DisvMesh.xt3d_reason): the triangle strip has a p95 connection non-orthogonality of 34 deg, above the 30 deg trigger, so XT3D is on; the Voronoi strip is orthogonal and runs with the two-point flux. Control run on the triangles with the two-point flux: 10.2 % instead of 2.7 %.

Tolerance rationale - tests/TOLERANCES.md row 7: NSE > 0.95 across all (x, t) probes with a maximum pointwise relative error below 2.5 % (measured 2.2 % at the production grid). The DISV strips measured 2.52 % (Voronoi, NSE 0.99979) and 2.71 % (triangles, NSE 0.99976) at the same cell size of 0.1 m, so they carry their own limits (DISV_BASE_LIMITS). The gap is the scheme's truncation error (TVD limiter and backward Euler at a Courant number of 0.5), not a mesh defect: the refinement test cuts it by a factor of about 4 on every grid (rectilinear 2.2 to 0.49 %, Voronoi 2.52 to 0.62 %, triangles 2.71 to 0.70 %). A second test refines dt by 4 and dx by 2 and requires the error to fall below that of the production run.

Scope - solver_sanity: The coupled GWF + GWT column with inlet auxiliary concentration is built directly on the flopy SDK because hydromodpy's transport plumbing does not yet expose MF6 GWT through the launcher TOML. The test therefore validates MODFLOW 6 GWT against the Ogata-Banks analytical solution, not the hydromodpy pipeline.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A fully penetrating well pumps at a constant rate Q in a homogeneous isotropic confined aquifer of transmissivity T and storativity S. The drawdown field is radial:

s(r, t) = Q / (4 pi T) * W(u),  u = r^2 S / (4 T t)

with well function W(u) = E_1(u) (exponential integral). The numerical reference is an MF6 IMS-backed confined GWF model. The grid is telescoping - a fine inner patch resolves the near-well drawdown and coarse outer cells push the Dirichlet boundary far enough that its influence on the observation window stays well below the test tolerance. Drawdown is evaluated at three radial distances (10 m, 50 m, 100 m) and three times (1 d, 3 d, 10 d) and compared pointwise against s(r, t).

Four grids run the same aquifer, well, time steps and probes:

* ``modflow6``: the MF6 telescoping rectilinear DIS grid above.
* ``modflow_nwt``: the same telescoping grid in MODFLOW-NWT (UPW, confined
 layer, ``ibound = -1`` on the outer ring, ``headtol = 1e-8`` m: the NWT
 default of 1e-2 m would hide a 1 % bound on drawdowns of a few decimeters).
* ``modflow6_irregular_tri`` and ``modflow6_voronoi``: DISV discs of
 jittered concentric rings (``tests/validation/helpers/disv_meshes.py``),
 cells growing by 1.2 per ring out to 9 km, the well in the cell that holds
 the origin, the head held in the cells with a boundary edge. The probe is
 the cell whose center is the closest to the target point and the closed
 form uses the discrete distance between the two centers.

XT3D on the triangles follows HydroModPy's rule (DisvMesh.xt3d_reason): the triangle disc has a p95 connection non-orthogonality of 37 deg, above the 30 deg trigger, so XT3D is on (control run with the two-point flux: 1.03 % instead of 0.66 %). The Voronoi disc is orthogonal and runs with the two-point flux.

Tolerance rationale - tests/TOLERANCES.md rows 4/5: * NSE against analytical drawdown must exceed 0.999. * Maximum absolute error across all (r, t) pairs: 1% relative.

Measured: rectilinear 0.44 %, NWT 0.44 % (NSE 0.99986 both), triangles 0.66 % (NSE 0.99990), Voronoi 2.08 % (NSE 0.99606). Rows 4 and 5 hold for the first three. The Voronoi disc keeps a gap of its own (DISV_LIMITS, 1.1 times the measurement). Control runs on the same Voronoi disc: the error comes from the ring step, not from the near-well cell or the jitter. Keeping ring growth 1.2 and moving the first ring from 1.0 to 0.5 m leaves 2.09 %; removing the jitter leaves 1.87 %; growth 1.1 gives 1.22 % (NSE 0.99936) and growth 1.05 gives 0.94 % (NSE 0.99974). At 10 d, the error at r = 100 m falls from 1.35 % to 0.42 % to 0.16 % over the three growths.

Scope - solver_sanity: The model is built directly on the flopy SDK (telescoping grid, central well, outer CHD ring) because the geometry sits outside what the hydromodpy launcher TOML exposes. This test therefore validates MODFLOW 6 against the Theis analytical solution, not the hydromodpy pipeline. It protects against solver-level regressions and bundled-binary drift, not against hydromodpy refactors. The NWT leg checks the NWT binary against the same closed form.

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 4: Theis confined pumping 2D, NSE vs analytical (9 probes): > 0.999 (Richardson, telescoping grid, 1 m near-well cell)
  • Row 5: Theis confined pumping 2D, max pointwise relative drawdown error: < 1 % (Near-well discretization, domain radius ≫ r_i(t = 10 d))

Test functions

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

End-to-end validation of HMP's home-grown DISV LAK build against the upstream MODFLOW 6 example. Patch test: a uniform flow on skewed triangles#

pass, known gap end to endmodflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_localmodflow6_irregular_tri_xt3d_offmodflow6_voronoi_generated

Known gap: modflow6_irregular_tri_xt3d_off

The two-point flux is not consistent on these triangles. It takes the flux across an edge as T L (h_b - h_a) / d, d the distance between the two cell centers: that is the flux of a uniform gradient only where the center line is normal to the edge. On this strip the angle between them has a median of 23 deg and a 95th percentile of 42 deg, so a linear head does not balance and the solution bends: 3 to 6 % of the head drop. Control run, the same files with XT3D: 6e-8 m. The error does not fall with the cell size: the Boussinesq solver, which has the same flux, reads 5.8e-3, 5.6e-3 and 5.5e-3 m RMSE on 80, 320 and 1280 triangles of the same shapes. Gmsh catchment meshes have such angles; HydroModPy switches XT3D on by itself when their 95th percentile passes 30 deg.

Known gap: boussinesq

The Boussinesq solver, on either engine, has a two-point flux between triangle centroids, T L (h_b - h_a) / d, d the distance between the centroids, with no correction for skewed cells. It is the flux of a uniform gradient only where the centroid line is normal to the edge. On this strip the angle between them has a median of 23 deg and a 95th percentile of 42 deg, so a linear head does not balance and the solution bends: 3 to 6 % of the head drop, as for MODFLOW 6 with XT3D off (5.7e-3 m). The error does not fall with the cell size: 5.8e-3, 5.6e-3 and 5.5e-3 m RMSE on 80, 320 and 1280 triangles of the same shapes, the mark of an inconsistent scheme. MODFLOW 6 with XT3D reproduces the head to 6e-8 m. A Gmsh catchment mesh has such angles; the island cases mesh near-equilateral triangles for this reason.

Known gap: boussinesq_local

The Boussinesq solver has a two-point flux between triangle centroids, T L (h_b - h_a) / d, d the distance between the centroids, with no correction for skewed cells. It is the flux of a uniform gradient only where the centroid line is normal to the edge. On this strip the angle between them has a median of 23 deg and a 95th percentile of 42 deg, so a linear head does not balance and the solution bends: 3 to 6 % of the head drop, as for MODFLOW 6 with XT3D off (5.7e-3 m). The error does not fall with the cell size: 5.8e-3, 5.6e-3 and 5.5e-3 m RMSE on 80, 320 and 1280 triangles of the same shapes, the mark of an inconsistent scheme. MODFLOW 6 with XT3D reproduces the head to 6e-8 m. A Gmsh catchment mesh has such angles; the island cases mesh near-equilateral triangles for this reason.

Not run on

  • NWT: MODFLOW-NWT builds a structured grid of axis-aligned rectangles and ignores a runtime mesh: it cannot hold the skewed triangles of this strip.
  • MF6: The structured MODFLOW 6 grid is axis-aligned rectangles with centres normal to the shared faces: no skewed cells. Its skewed-triangle runs are the triangle and Voronoi columns.

Compared with: the steady head of a uniform flow at every triangle centroid.

\[\left(h(x)-z_b\right)^2=\left(h_W-z_b\right)^2+\left[\left(h_E-z_b\right)^2-\left(h_W-z_b\right)^2\right]\frac{x-x_W}{x_E-x_W}\]

Why these thresholds

  • Thresholds of boussinesq: 1.1 times the measurement, a documented gap (below): RMSE 0.0058 m, max error 0.0131 m, for a head drop of 0.2 m across the strip. The PETSc engine assembles the residual of the default local engine (the shared two-point flux) and agrees with it to 1e-13 m, so both carry the same bound.
  • Thresholds of boussinesq_local: 1.1 times the measurement, a documented gap (below): RMSE 0.0058 m, max error 0.0131 m, for a head drop of 0.2 m across the strip.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri: Derived. XT3D reconstructs the gradient from the neighbors and is exact for a uniform flow on any cell shape: what is left is the solver closure (outer dvclose 1e-9 m) and the spread of the transmissivity, 2e-4 across the strip, which moves the exact head off a straight line by 5e-6 m. The bound is twice that. Measured: RMSE 2.3e-8 m, max 5.8e-8 m.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_irregular_tri_xt3d_off: 1.1 times the measurement, a documented gap (below): RMSE 0.0057 m, max error 0.0120 m, for a head drop of 0.2 m across the strip.
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi: Twice the measurement: RMSE 3.9e-8 m, max error 7.3e-8 m. The Voronoi dual of the skewed nodes has orthogonal cells (a face bisects the two nodes it separates), so the two-point flux of a uniform gradient is exact, as XT3D is on the triangles. What is left is the solver closure (outer dvclose 1e-9 m) and the 2e-4 spread of the transmissivity across the strip. The heads are held on the nodes of the faces, x = 0 and 100 m, and the reference is anchored there. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: heads.rmse 8e-8 (measure 3.94e-8, patch test: solver closure and the spread of T); heads.max_abs_error 1.5e-7 (measure 7.28e-8, patch test: solver closure and the spread of T).
  • Thresholds of modflow6_voronoi_generated: Twice the measurement: RMSE 2.58e-8 m, max error 6.35e-8 m. The engine generates the mesh of the 100 x 40 m strip (no triangulation read): its cells are orthogonal to their faces (a face bisects the two seeds it separates), so the two-point flux of a uniform gradient is exact. What is left is the solver closure (outer dvclose 1e-9 m) and the 2e-4 spread of the transmissivity across the strip. The contact at x = 50 m is a mirror-pair face between two zones of the same K, so it changes nothing. Measured 2026-10-14. B9 of the unified mesh, measured again on 2026-10-26. Kept at a numerical floor, where twice the measure guarantees nothing: heads.rmse 5.2e-8 (measure 2.59e-8, patch test: solver closure and the spread of T); heads.max_abs_error 1.3e-7 (measure 6.48e-8, patch test: solver closure and the spread of T).

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A consistent finite-volume flux reproduces a linear head on any cell shape. On this strip of skewed, non-isosceles triangles MODFLOW 6 with XT3D does, to the solver closure, and so does MODFLOW 6 on the Voronoi dual of the same nodes and on a Voronoi mesh generated on the same strip: the cells are orthogonal to their faces (the face between two cells bisects their nodes), so the two-point flux of a uniform gradient is exact. The two-point flux between triangle centroids, in MODFLOW 6 without XT3D and in the Boussinesq solver (default local engine and PETSc engine, which assemble the same residual), does not: their error is recorded against a documented gap.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

The SAME transient multi-layer lake-aquifer problem (Plainfield Lakes abacus, one reservoir incised across the top two layers of a 4-layer aquifer) is solved through the production HMP LAK builders and MF6 on three grids:

  • REGULAR: the 15x15 quad DISV (225 cells, 40 m), the reference. It has its own test, which checks that it closes its LAK water balance.
  • TRIANGLE: a refined Delaunay triangle DISV (~772 cells, ~20 m near the lake).
  • VORONOI: a ragged Voronoi DISV (372 cells of 4 to 9 edges, 20 m over the lake), the default HydroModPy grid. Its edges run along the lake polygon, so the lake footprint is the same 200 m x 200 m.

Only the mesh changes: the domain, layers, lake footprint, abacus, bedleak, aquifer K / recharge, TDIS and per-period rainfall / evaporation / runoff are shared. The cross-grid test, run once per irregular grid, asserts:

  • the irregular grid is a genuine non-rectangular mesh that resolves the lake at least as finely as the quad grid;
  • the per-period lake stages agree within the documented stage envelope;
  • the steady lake-aquifer exchange flux agrees within the documented envelope;
  • both grids close their LAK water balance.

A materially diverging grid (wrong CONNECTIONDATA geometry, lost bank seepage) would break the stage envelope by an order of magnitude. The Voronoi stage gap (0.054 m, against 0.038 m for the triangles) is the cell size at the lake bank, not the builder: see tolerances_grid_equivalence_voronoi.toml.

The HMP package-agnostic MVR seam (MoverRecord -> build_mvr_period_records -> mover_package_count -> packages list, the exact assembly build.py performs) drives the upstream example's four transfers: two SFR -> LAK feeds and two LAK -> SFR spillway releases (one at FACTOR 0.5). Two levels:

  • STRUCTURAL: the HMP-formatted MVR period block reproduces the published mvr_spd rows verbatim and counts two packages;
  • NUMERICAL: real MF6 converges and the final lake stages match the PUBLISHED values (116.98 / 111.93 ft) within the documented tolerances.toml band, with all four transfers carrying water and the budget closed.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

Governing PDE on [0, 1] with Dirichlet 0/0 and initial condition h(x, 0) = sin(pi x):

h_t - D h_xx = 0

The manufactured solution h(x, t) = exp(-pi^2 D t) sin(pi x) is an exact eigenfunction of the Laplacian with no forcing. The discretization combines the standard second-order centered-space stencil with either backward Euler (first-order in time) or Crank-Nicolson (second-order in time) for the temporal update. Two refinement studies are run:

  • space - dx refined with Crank-Nicolson in time so the temporal error stays small enough for the spatial slope to emerge. Expected slope ~2.
  • time - dx held fine, dt refined under backward Euler. Expected slope ~1 (see tests/TOLERANCES.md row 10).

Scope, read this before citing the result ----------------------------------------- This file imports nothing from hydromodpy. It verifies the *scheme* on a stencil assembled inside the test, which is what MMS is for: it establishes that the discretization written here converges at its theoretical order. It does not exercise HydroModPy's own assembly, so a passing run here is not evidence that the production discretization is second-order.

What does cover the production path is the analytical tier (tests/validation/analytical/): Theis, Hantush and Ogata-Banks run a real solve through HydroModPy and compare against a closed form. Those would catch a gross regression, but a silent drop from order 2 to order 1 that stays inside the RMSE band would pass them. Closing that gap means running this convergence study on the production assembly, not extending this file.

Test functions

  • Mms diffusion transient space converges at order two.
  • Mms diffusion transient time converges at order one.

File tests/validation/mms/test_mms_diffusion_transient.py. Markers: analytical, fast, transient, validation.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

Manufactured solution on [0, 1] with Dirichlet 0/0 boundaries:

u_exact(x) = sin(pi x)
-u''(x)    = pi^2 sin(pi x) = f(x)

The vertex-centered finite-volume (equivalent to the standard second-order centered finite-difference) stencil is:

(u[i-1] - 2 u[i] + u[i+1]) / h^2 = -f[i]

which is second-order consistent. Running on a sequence of refinements and regressing log ||e||_2 against log h gives an empirical order expected to sit inside [1.8, 2.2] (see tests/TOLERANCES.md row 8).

Scope, read this before citing the result ----------------------------------------- This file imports nothing from hydromodpy. It verifies the *scheme* on a stencil assembled inside the test, which is what MMS is for: it establishes that the discretization written here converges at its theoretical order. It does not exercise HydroModPy's own assembly, so a passing run here is not evidence that the production discretization is second-order.

What does cover the production path is the analytical tier (tests/validation/analytical/): Theis, Hantush and Ogata-Banks run a real solve through HydroModPy and compare against a closed form. Those would catch a gross regression, but a silent drop from order 2 to order 1 that stays inside the RMSE band would pass them. Closing that gap means running this convergence study on the production assembly, not extending this file.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A run with K = 2e-4, 5e-5 and 1e-4 m/s in three bands of a fixed-head strip gives three heads and the east outlet discharge. Each method then searches the three K from those four series alone. The twin runs on MODFLOW-NWT, MODFLOW 6 on its structured grid, on a triangle mesh and on the Voronoi dual of that mesh, and on the Boussinesq solver on the same triangles, with its PETSc engine and with its default local engine. The truth and the trials of a column come from the same solver, so the twin tests the recovery on each discretization and not the solver itself. The Boussinesq trials read the state history of the solver, and the outlet discharge is the flux through the fixed-head cells. The PETSc leg skips CMA-ES when the cma package is missing from its environment: the other four runs exercise the forward model alike. A second test checks that the twin is closed: with the search started at the truth, the cost and the error are zero on every column.

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 154: Twin calibration closure, noise free, search started at the truth (piecewise K, transient K+Sy; MODFLOW-NWT, MODFLOW 6, MODFLOW 6 triangles, MODFLOW 6 Voronoi), best normalized cost, and |p - p_true| / p_true of every parameter, after 3 evaluations of Nelder-Mead: <= 1e-12 (Machine epsilon. The bounds are symmetric about the truth with a uniform prior on the identity transform, so the first trial is the truth up to one rounding of (lo + hi) / 2. The truth observations (catalog Run, field_precision = "exact") and the trial observations (solver files) are then the same numbers at the same cell)

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

The truth runs on a mesh twice as fine as the calibration mesh, so the recovered K carries the discretization error of the solver. A fixed-head Dupuit strip gives the head at mid-length and the east outlet discharge. The structured columns (MODFLOW-NWT, MODFLOW 6) compare 80 by 5 cells with 40 by 5. The triangle column compares a 750-triangle bundle with the 176-triangle bundle of the analytical case, and the Voronoi column the duals of the two. The two Boussinesq columns, the PETSc engine and the default local engine, use the same two triangle bundles. The recovery is asserted within 2.5e-5 m/s of the true 1e-4 m/s. The PETSc leg skips CMA-ES when the cma package is missing from its environment.

Steady same-solver twin benchmark for calibration#

pass modflow6

Not run on

  • NWT, MF6 triangles, MF6 Voronoi: The only observable is the east boundary flux, which is exactly proportional to K for fixed heads and no sources, so the normalized cost and the recovery do not depend on the solver. Measured on NWT, MF6 triangles and MF6 Voronoi: grid, random search, Optuna and CMA-ES return identical errors.
  • Boussinesq: The only observable is the east boundary flux, which is exactly proportional to K for fixed heads and no sources, so the normalized cost and the recovery do not depend on the solver. The head stays far below the surface, so the Boussinesq obstacle closure never acts.
  • Boussinesq default: The only observable is the east boundary flux, which is exactly proportional to K for fixed heads and no sources, so the normalized cost and the recovery do not depend on the solver. The head stays far below the surface, so the surface closure never acts.

Compared with: the parameter values that generated the synthetic observations of the twin experiment.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A run with K = 1e-4 m/s and Sy = 0.10 under a recharge step gives the head at mid-aquifer and the outlet discharge. Each method then searches K in [5e-5, 3e-4] and Sy in [0.04, 0.18] from those two series alone. This is the one well-posed two-parameter transient calibration of the suite: the head series constrains Sy and the discharge series constrains K. It runs on MODFLOW-NWT, MODFLOW 6 on its structured grid, on a triangle mesh and on the Voronoi dual of that mesh, and on the Boussinesq solver on the same triangles. The Boussinesq PETSc leg runs the six methods, minus CMA-ES when the cma package is missing from its environment. The default local engine leg is slow, so it runs Nelder-Mead and Optuna, two of the asserted methods. CMA-ES, Nelder-Mead and Optuna are asserted to land within the case tolerance of the truth (1.5e-5 on K, 0.04 on Sy). Random search, GP mapping and DA-MH-GP also run; their distances to the truth are recorded for information and not asserted, because their budget does not guarantee a hit on a smooth two-parameter surface.

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 154: Twin calibration closure, noise free, search started at the truth (piecewise K, transient K+Sy; MODFLOW-NWT, MODFLOW 6, MODFLOW 6 triangles, MODFLOW 6 Voronoi), best normalized cost, and |p - p_true| / p_true of every parameter, after 3 evaluations of Nelder-Mead: <= 1e-12 (Machine epsilon. The bounds are symmetric about the truth with a uniform prior on the identity transform, so the first trial is the truth up to one rounding of (lo + hi) / 2. The truth observations (catalog Run, field_precision = "exact") and the trial observations (solver files) are then the same numbers at the same cell)

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

test_twin_matching_stream_network_modflow6.py runs one row of cells that drains 0.0016 km2, so it has to force the crossing rule. This twin runs what protocol 1.3 freezes and writes no key of its network output: the heads rule, the map cut to the catchment, the catchment bound, D8 where the mesh has corners.

The basin is a comb on a DEM, 80 by 70 cells of 20 m. A main stem runs east to the outlet on the border, and five straight valleys join it, three from the north and two from the south, each with its own slope, so their heads do not move at the same K. Each valley is a V whose talweg runs through cell centers, with sides steep enough to keep the seepage on the talweg: the flow toward a talweg, about R * 300 m, stays below what the full aquifer carries down a side, K * 30 m * 0.06. The simulated network is then one cell wide, like the trace of a head, so the map can equal it cell for cell. On a wider network the map could not, and this would measure that width and not the rule.

At K/R = 600 the run makes six heads, one per valley and one on the main stem, each draining more than 0.02 km2 and inside its valley. The map holds one line per head, from that head down the descent to the first confluence, and the main stem runs on for 200 m past the outlet, so the cut to the catchment makes one more free end that must not count. A network-only search under the protocol must return that K.

A pass proves little on its own, so the twin also has to fail. A map drawn at another K must give that K. A map with a head missing, heads placed low or a map 200 m off must each fail, and each row names the checks it fails. Heads all moved south shorten three valleys and lengthen two, which keeps K in its band, so D_optim is a check of its own: J balances and the distances do not vanish. Below the heads, the path of a line must not count: a map that wanders off the talwegs gives the same K, and the same map under the crossing rule does not.

One search widens its bounds past the physical ceiling of K, 100 m/s: its trial there is infeasible, gets the failed cost and leaves the failure streak alone, so the search walks out and closes.

A generated triangle mesh is left out, see NOT_APPLICABLE. On a Voronoi mesh the cells follow the talwegs of the DEM drawn at 0.02 km2, a threshold set a priori and never read from the map, and the map is drawn from that run. Tolerances: tests/TOLERANCES.md, rows 184 to 186, and row 79 for the ratios.

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 184: Twin stream-network calibration under heads (MF6, comb basin, 5600 cells of 20 m, six heads), |K - K_true| / K_true at the returned trial: <= 3 % (Derived. The bisection stops on a bracket no wider than log10(1.01), and it closes on the zero plateau of J, the K range that reproduces the mapped network cell for cell. That plateau runs from 5.99e-6 to 6.10e-6 m/s around K_true = 6e-6 m/s, so up to 1.9 % above it, and a trial off the plateau is the end of a bracket that holds it, so 1 % further. One head moves one cell per 3 % of K, so the plateau is that step shared between five heads and this band is about one step)
  • Row 185: Twin stream-network calibration under heads (MF6), D_optim at the returned trial: <= 1 m (Derived. Over the band of row 184 the simulated network differs from the map by at most five cells, each a cell or two from it, averaged over 124 cells: the sweep reads 0.31 m at -1.4 % and 0.40 m at +2.9 %. The band is 2.5 times that, a twentieth of a cell. It exists because a balanced J does not say the two networks agree)
  • Row 186: Twin stream-network calibration under heads (MF6), d_sat_m of the returned trial over the truth run: rel <= 1.1e-2 (Derived. The sweep gives d dsat / d ln K of -6.4 m around the truth on a mean of 17.9 m, so the 3 % of row 184 moves dsat by 0.19 m, 1.07 % of it)
  • Row 79: Twin stream-network calibration (MF6), k_optim_m_s, k_over_r, t_over_r_m, t_optim_m2_s against K, R_mean_m_s and d_sat_m of the returned trial: rel 1e-12 (Machine epsilon. Each is one product or quotient of values the report read off that trial)

Test functions

  • The map holds the known heads and traces back to the network.
  • A search under the protocol recovers the conductivity that made the heads.
  • A wrong map or a wrong head count fails the twin.
  • A map drawn at another conductivity gives that conductivity.
  • Below its head the path of a line counts under crossing only.
  • A search walks out of the infeasible trial it crosses.
  • A map whose every head is lost is refused before the first solve.
  • Two maps read k and leave sy within one cell.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

A model run with a known conductivity produces a seepage network. That network, written as the mapped one, must bring a network-only bisection back to the conductivity that produced it. Nothing else in the suite runs the criterion end to end on a real solve: the unit tests fake the trial context, and a real catchment has no known answer.

The catchment is a planar hillslope, one row of 400 square cells of 2 m, over a 30 m aquifer parallel to the surface. Under uniform recharge R the water table reaches the surface where the recharge collected upslope exceeds what the full aquifer can carry, K * d * slope: the seepage face starts at about K d s / R from the divide, so the network retracts by one cell per cell / (K d s / R) of relative K, about 0.56 per cent here. That step is the resolution of the criterion. It is kept below the one per cent the bisection stops on, so the recovered value can be held to that one per cent whether the search lands on the zero plateau or closes its bracket around it.

The drains sit on the surface with the fallback conductance, proportional to K, which is what makes the network a function of K/R alone. The mapped network is the downstream closure of the seepage cells, built by the same functions the criterion calls, and its round trip through the GPKG back onto the mesh is checked cell for cell before any calibration runs. The round trip goes through the resolver and observed_network_mask under the crossing rule, the route a map.complete takes in a calibration trial. The calibration sets that rule: the default, heads, needs a drained area this hillslope never reaches, and test_twin_matching_stream_heads_modflow6.py runs that default on a basin that does.

What this twin cannot see: on a single row no two network cells meet only at a corner, so the crossing and the touch rules give the same mask here. The diagonal-step bias the crossing rule exists to remove is covered by the unit tests of line_crossing_cell_mask, not by this experiment.

Four solver columns run the same hillslope. MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 on its structured grid use the 400 square cells. The triangle column splits each of those squares into two triangles of the same strip (800 cells), and the Voronoi column puts a cell on each node of that triangulation (802 cells, two rows of nodes on the strip borders). On an unstructured mesh the mapped network is the polyline through the cell centers of the reach, in order downslope, which the crossing rule gives back cell for cell. The centers are the polygon centroids of the triangles and the generator nodes of the Voronoi cells, the points the criterion samples the top at. The 30 m aquifer, the slope and the recharge are the same, so the seepage face starts near the same 357 m from the divide. The two rows of Voronoi nodes sit at one elevation and do not drain into each other, so the criterion scores the catchment of one row, 401 of the 802 cells.

Tolerances: tests/TOLERANCES.md, rows 76 to 79, for every column. They are properties of the criterion, a bisection to one per cent on a network drawn on the cells, and not of the solver.

Thresholds from tests/TOLERANCES.md

  • Row 76: Twin stream-network calibration (MF6, planar hillslope, 400 cells of 2 m), |K - K_true| / K_true at the returned trial, and the same on k_over_r against K_true / R: <= 1 % (Derived. The bisection stops on a bracket no wider than log10(1.01). The zero plateau of J, the K range that reproduces the mapped network cell for cell, is one cell over the length of the unsaturated slope, cell / (K d s / R) = 2 m / 357 m = 0.56 %, measured between 5.99e-6 and 6.03e-6 m/s. A returned trial on the plateau is within 0.56 % of K_true; one off it is an end of a closed bracket that holds the plateau, so within 1 %)
  • Row 78: Twin stream-network calibration (MF6), d_sat_m at the returned trial against the truth run: rel <= 1e-3 (Derived. The sweep gives d dsat / d ln K of about 1.06 m around the truth, so 1 % on K moves dsat by 0.011 m, 3.6e-4 of 29.47 m; the band is 2.8 times that)
  • Row 79: Twin stream-network calibration (MF6), k_optim_m_s, k_over_r, t_over_r_m, t_optim_m2_s against K, R_mean_m_s and d_sat_m of the returned trial: rel 1e-12 (Machine epsilon. Each is one product or quotient of values the report read off that trial)

  • The mapped network projects back onto the cells it was written from.
  • A network only bisection recovers the conductivity that made the network.

Two solvers on one catchment#

The cases above compare each solver with an exact solution. A catchment has none, so the reference model of example 04 is run twice from the same file: once with MODFLOW 6, once with MODFLOW-NWT. Only the solver of the flow process changes. Both runs store their fields at full precision: the default compact storage rounds these heads to steps of 1 to 2 mm, more than the gap between the two solvers. tools/docs/figures/render_ex04_figures.py (group solvers) makes both runs and draws the figures below; tools/docs/figures/figures.toml keeps the command behind each one.

The aquifer of example 04 has the same thickness in every cell. Where the thickness changes from one cell to the next, MODFLOW 6 under Newton computes another horizontal conductance than MODFLOW-NWT, smaller where water flows from a thicker cell to a thinner one. MODFLOW 6 then reads a computational top that gives every cell the same thickness, and the two solvers agree again: the circular-island cases above show it on the Cartesian grid.
